☆ Existence and Uniqueness of Mild Solutions to Rough Stochastic Partial Differential Equations driven by Fractional Brownian Motion with Hurst Index $H > 1/4$
Maksim Vaskouski, Maksim Firsau
In this paper we prove a theorem on the unique solvability of the Cauchy problem for a stochastic partial differential equation driven by the fractional Brownian motion with Hurst index $H>\frac{1}{4}$.
☆ Global regularity in optimal transportation under the A3w condition
Yuanyuan Li, Xianduo Wang, Xu-jia Wang
We prove global $C^{2,α}$ and $W^{2,p}$ estimates for potentials in optimal transportation under A3w condition. The cost satisfies condition A3w, and the domains are mutually uniformly $c$-convex with $C^2$ boundaries. We prove global $W^{2,p}$ estimates for positive continuous densities and we obtain global $C^{2,α}$ estimates for positive $C^α$ densities.
☆ Existence and uniqueness for a coagulation-transport equation
Edwin Aguilar Anzures, L. F. López Ríos, Arno Siri-Jégousse
This paper establishes the existence, uniqueness, and regularity of weak solutions to a class of nonlinear coagulation-transport equations describing the asymptotic dynamics of multispecies coalescent processes. The model captures the multi-scale ancestral lineage decay governed by an autonomous drift field, coupled with a time-inhomogeneous quadratic coagulation term parameterized by the initial population mass. By utilizing the metric structure of probability measures, we demonstrate that any weak solution satisfies a unique mild representation formula dictated by the transport semigroup. This characterization allows us to construct a unified narrative where existence, uniqueness, and moment preservation are proved directly through a contractive fixed-point argument in the space of finite Radon measures.
☆ Spectral asymptotics for vector-valued magnetic Schrödinger operators
Vincenzo Leone, Marianna Porfido, Abdelaziz Rhandi
We consider vector-valued magnetic Schrödinger operators $-Δ_{a} +V$ with magnetic potential ${a}\in C^2(\mathbb{R}^d;\mathbb{R}^d)$ and electric potential $V$ given by a symmetric and positive semidefinite $m\times m$ matrix-valued function whose entries belong to $L^1_{\rm loc}(\mathbb{R}^d)$. Assuming that $\|\operatorname{curl} {a}(\cdot)\|\operatorname{Id}_{\mathbb{R}^m} + V$ belongs to a certain matrix reverse Hölder class, we characterize necessary and sufficient conditions under which the spectrum of $-Δ_{a} +V$ is discrete, and study the eigenvalue asymptotics and exponential decay of eigenfunctions.
☆ Global existence versus blow-up for Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou lattices
Gerald Teschl, Anton Zand
This paper investigates the global behavior of infinite nonlinear lattices. In particular, for the Fermi--Pasta--Ulam--Tsingou-$α$ lattice (FPUT-$α$), we show global existence for small initial data via a region-based approach, and prove blow-up for negative energy and some positive energy, given appropriate conditions on the initial momentum and dispersion. Moreover, we extend these results to the nonlinear Klein-Gordon (DNKG) equation and nonlinear wave (DNW) equation. \

☆ Nondegeneracy and uniqueness of ground states of the Schrödinger equation with Neumann conditions in a weakly nonlocal regime
Serena Dipierro, María Medina, Enrico Valdinoci
We consider the nonlocal Schrödinger equation driven by a fractional Laplacian of order~$2s$, with~$s$ close to~$1$. Differently from the existing literature, which focused on either global problems in the whole of~$\R^n$ or Dirichlet conditions, we study here the case of nonlocal Neumann conditions in the halfspace. Moreover, we prove that ground states are nondegenerate, i.e. the only solutions of the linearized equation are linear combinations of the tangential derivatives of the ground state. Consequently, the ground state is unique, up to tangential translations and a change of sign.
☆ First Neumann eigenfunctions on piecewise smooth Jordan domains with convex corners
Santiago Pineda Montoya, Edisson Gallego González, Jaiberth Porras Barrera, Johan H. Rúa Muñoz
We prove that every nonzero eigenfunction of the first positive Neumann eigenvalue on a bounded planar Jordan domain whose boundary consists of finitely many smooth arcs meeting at interior angles strictly between $0$ and $π$ has nonvanishing gradient in the interior; hence its extrema are attained only on the boundary. The eigenvalue may be multiple and the domain need not be convex; every convex polygon is included. The method adapts a recent Green-kernel approach for smooth domains.

☆ Global-in-time maximal regularity for the Dunkl heat equation in BMO
Xuejing Huo, Ming-Yi Lee, Chaojie Wen, Liangchuan Wu
We establish global-in-time maximal regularity for the Cauchy problem of the Dunkl heat equation in BMO, without assuming reflection invariance of the external force. For a Hilbert-valued BMO function $F$, we integrate the spatial mean-square oscillation of the Dunkl gradient of its heat extension over all $t>0$ on each fixed Euclidean ball. The supremum of these integrals is comparable to the squared BMO seminorm of $F$. In particular, the upper estimates imply time-weighted energy estimates for the zero-initial-value solution and maximal regularity for nonzero initial values whose weak Dunkl derivatives belong to BMO.
☆ A non-zero gap for the planar Mumford-Shah convex lifting and the nonexistence of crack-tip calibrations
Marcello Carioni, Giorgio Patrini
We prove that the convex lifting of the Mumford-Shah functional constructed through the notion of calibration introduced in [2] is not sharp in dimension two. For Dirichlet boundary data prescribed by the crack-tip function, we construct a lifted competitor whose energy is strictly lower than that of the crack-tip subgraph. Since the crack-tip minimizes the original Mumford-Shah functional, this establishes a strict gap between the infima of the original and lifted problems. As a consequence we establish that the crack-tip admits no calibration.
☆ Sheetwise stationarity for stationary unions of $C^{1,α}$ graphs
Mattia Luchese
We prove that stationarity of a finite union of $C^{1,α}$ graphs implies stationarity of each individual graph, in arbitrary dimension and codimension. The proof closely follows the approach of Minter and Stanbury \cite{MinterStanbury}, who also raised this question in their Remark~1.6. As in their paper, we give a proof that uses the planar frequency results of Krummel, Minter and Wickramasekera \cite{KMW26} (but avoids the centre manifold construction of that paper). We also rely on the Schauder estimates for $Q$-valued functions established in \cite{Luc26}.
☆ Perturbation Algorithm and Iterative Realization of a Four-Layer Semi-Discrete Scheme for an Evolutionary Problem with a Variable Operator
David Gulua, Jemal Rogava, Zurab Vashakidze
In a Hilbert space, we consider the Cauchy problem for an evolutionary equation with the operator $A+B(t)$, where $A$ is a self-adjoint positive definite operator and $B(t)$ is a bounded operator depending on time. By means of the perturbation algorithm, the purely implicit four-layer semi-discrete scheme of the third order of approximation (the three-step backward differentiation formula) is reduced to three two-layer schemes, whose solutions are used to construct an approximate solution of the original problem. In each two-layer scheme, the term containing $B(t)$ is moved to the right-hand side, and the resulting equation is solved by an iterative method, so that only the time-independent operator $I+τA$ has to be inverted; the convergence of the iterations at the rate of a geometric progression with a ratio of order $τ$ is proved. A priori estimates for the two-layer and four-layer schemes are obtained by means of a discrete analogue of Gronwall's lemma. An estimate of order $τ^3$ for the error of the approximate solution is proved under an assumption on the difference quotients of the computed grid functions on the first layers. The results are illustrated by numerical experiments.

☆ Large time decay of the fluid-structure semigroup subject to the Navier slip-with-friction boundary condition
Toshiaki Hishida, Bum Ja Jin
Consider the motion of a rigid body moving into a viscous incompressible fluid that fills the whole space in 3D. The fluid motion obeys the Navier-Stokes system, while the motion of the body is governed by the Newton law. Both motions are affected by each other at the fluid-solid interface through the Navier slip-with-friction boundary condition, which is known as a substitution for the no-slip one to resolve the no-collision paradox. We adopt a monolithic approach and carry out the spectral analysis to deduce the large time behavior of the fluid-structure semigroup, where the shape of the body is allowed to be arbitrary. What is remarkable is that the decay structure is somewhat different under the full slip condition when the body is axially symmetric. If, in particular, the body is a ball, we then apply the linear theory developed above to the nonlinear initial value problem to show the stability of the rest state. It is, furthermore, asymptotically stable except for the full slip case.

☆ A variational theory for von Kármán vortex streets
In-Jee Jeong, Guolin Qin, Kwan Woo
We construct von Kármán vortex streets as global kinetic energy maximizers for the 2D Euler flow in an infinite periodic channel: our variational framework imposes no a prior symmetry, support constraints, or sign conditions on the admissible class. More specifically, under $O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ constraint of the absolute vorticity maximum with other natural constraints, we show that the maximizers are traveling pairs of simply connected vortex patches of support radius $O(\varepsilon)$, converging to the von Kármán point-vortex configuration satisfying glide reflection symmetry as $\varepsilon \to 0$. We prove nonlinear stability of the von Kármán streets under a bound on the vertical support, using a compactness result valid for more general assumptions. Furthermore, we construct slightly tilted asymmetric von Kármán vortex streets as energy maximizers under a tilted moment constraint.

For a smooth axially symmetric function on $\mathbb{S}^n$ with $n\geq 1$, in odd dimensions we prove a neat formula for the critical nonlocal GJMS operator $P_n$ similar to the one in even dimensions. ☆ A family of homogeneous convex non-scattering domains with analytic non-circular boundaries
Fioralba Cakoni, Michael Levitin
A homogeneous planar non-scattering domain is a bounded medium with a constant material coefficient that produces no scattered field for some nonzero entire solution of the Helmholtz equation at a particular wave number. It is known that the boundary of such a domain must be real analytic at all points where the incident field does not vanish. Previously, disks were the only known examples. We construct a family of homogeneous strictly convex non-scattering domains that are neither disks nor ellipses. The family bifurcates from a particular non-scattering disk, with the boundary, wave number, and constant coefficient varying along the branch. The construction uses a conformal change of variables and analytic bifurcation theory applied to the resulting nonlinear problem.

☆ A note on a nonlocal antisymmetric barrier
Serena Dipierro, Giorgio Poggesi, Jack Thompson, Enrico Valdinoci
In this note, we present a barrier function for an equation involving the fractional Laplacian in the antisymmetric setting, providing an explicit inequality in the full positivity set of the function. This leads to an improvement of the quantitative maximum principle given in [DPTV26], where the bound was obtained in a strict subset of its positivity set and required additional assumptions on lower order coefficients. As a consequence of this, we give an optimal lower bound on the growth of antisymmetric solutions from the symmetry hyperplane.
☆ A One-Sided Liouville Theorem and a Critical Sparse-Support Inverse Theorem for Discrete Harmonic Functions
Xiyu Hu
We answer the one-sided Liouville question of Buhovsky, Logunov, Malinnikova, and Sodin (Duke Math. J. 171 (2022), Remark 1.4). There is an absolute $\varepsilon>0$ such that a real harmonic function on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ is constant if it is nonnegative on at least a $1-\varepsilon$ proportion of every sufficiently large centered square. More generally, for every nonconstant real harmonic function and every $a\le b$, the sets $\{ub\}$ each occupy a fixed positive proportion of the same arbitrarily large centered squares. Turning from sign conditions to sparse supports, we prove in three dimensions a local inverse theorem at the critical quadratic support scale. Write $Q_R=[-R,R]^3\cap\mathbb{Z}^3$. If a complex-valued function is harmonic in $Q_{30R}$ and has at most $AR^2$ nonzero values there, its support in $Q_R$ lies in at most $K_A$ characteristic planes $x_i\pm x_j=c$. The minimum number $m_3(N)$ of nonzero values in $Q_N$ among whole-lattice harmonic functions nonzero at the origin satisfies $m_3(N)=(1+o(1))(2N+1)^2$. More generally, if a fixed nonzero harmonic function on $\mathbb{Z}^3$ has $O(N^2)$ nonzero values in $Q_N$ along a sequence $N\to\infty$, then its support has a unique irredundant cover by finitely many characteristic planes. If there are $k$ such planes, the support count in $Q_N$ is $k(2N+1)^2+O_u(N)$.

☆ Determination of the unbounded potential of the Robin Laplacian from fixed-time boundary measurements of time-fractional diffusion-wave equations
Abdelmalek Metidji, Yacine Mokhtari
We consider the time-fractional diffusion-wave equation $\partial_t^ρu - Δu + q u = 0$ in a bounded domain $Ω\subset \RR^n$, $n \geq 3$, where $\partial_t^ρ$ is the Caputo derivative of arbitrary order $ρ\in (0,2)$. This framework covers in a unified way the sub-diffusive case $ρ\in (0,1)$, the classical heat equation $ρ= 1$, and the super-diffusive case $ρ\in (1,2)$. The real-valued potential $q$ is only assumed to lie in $L^{n/2}(Ω)$, and the equation is endowed with zero initial conditions and a non-homogeneous Robin boundary condition, whose coefficient is allowed to be unbounded as well. The boundary excitations are supported in an arbitrary open subset $Γ_0$ of the boundary, and the trace of the solution is measured, at one fixed time, on another open subset $Γ_1$. We prove that the corresponding Robin-to-Dirichlet map uniquely determines the boundary spectral data of the underlying Robin Laplacian on $Γ_0 \cup Γ_1$, provided that $Γ_0$ and $Γ_1$ overlap. When $Γ_0 \cup Γ_1$ is the whole boundary, we deduce that $q$ is uniquely determined by this map in every dimension $n \geq 3$, the critical case $q \in L^{3/2}(Ω)$ in dimension three being included. The proof combines analytic continuation in the time variable, the Laplace transform and an identification of the poles and residues of meromorphic functions. The potential is then recovered from the boundary spectral data through an elliptic Robin-to-Dirichlet map, an integral identity, and complex geometric optics solutions.
☆ Shrinking Limit for the Stationary Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation on Cross-Shaped Infinite Domains
Boris Shakarov
We study the stationary nonlinear Schrödinger equation on a planar, cross-shaped infinite domain and in the shrinking limit. For any fixed thickness, we establish the existence of solutions through a variational approach. To overcome the loss of compactness inherent to the unbounded geometry and bypass the regularity obstructions caused by the re-entrant corners, we constrain the minimization problem to a cone of symmetric and monotonic functions. We then establish the resolvent-preservation property, ensuring the constrained minimizers are stationary solutions. As the transverse width vanishes, we establish a transverse collapse phenomenon, that is, the two-dimensional solutions flatten across the central junction and become purely one-dimensional along the infinite branches. In this way, we prove that cross solutions converge strongly to a stationary solution on the limiting graph in a suitable sense. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this dimensional reduction recovers both vertex continuity and the Kirchhoff conditions.
☆ Global renormalized finite-energy weak solutions to the three-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes system on tori for $γ>4/3$
Guangyi Hong, Hongyun Peng, Changjiang Zhu
Building on the foundational theory of finite-energy weak solutions initiated by P.-L. Lions and further developed by E. Feireisl and collaborators, we establish the global existence of finite-energy renormalized weak solutions to the compressible Navier--Stokes equations on the three-dimensional torus, with constant viscosity coefficients and pressure law \(P(ρ)=ρ^γ\), for every \(γ>4/3\) and arbitrary finite-energy initial data. This extends the classical three-dimensional Lions--Feireisl existence theory beyond the threshold \(γ>3/2\), and in particular, covers the important case $ γ=7/5 $ for air (cf. \cite{Anderson}). Compared to the classical theory, we develop a novel approach to establish the improved pressure-integrability estimate compatible with the viscous and inertial terms, via constructing a periodic test field through barycentric optimal transport. This improved pressure-integrability estimate, combined with an effective viscous flux identity and an entropy comparison, provides the compactness needed to identify the nonlinear limits and recover the energy inequality.

☆ Asymptotic behavior of solutions to the one-dimensional $p$-system with time-dependent non-smooth damping
Toi Fujimura, Motohiro Sobajima
This paper is concerned with the asymptotic behavior of solutions to the Cauchy problem for the one-dimensional $p$-system with time-dependent damping. When the damping coefficient $b(t)$ behaves like $(1+t)^{-λ}$ with $0\leλ<1$, the solutions are expected to converge to a diffusion wave. For $b(t)=(1+t)^{-λ}$, previous studies have established convergence to a diffusion wave together with convergence rates using the energy method, provided that the initial perturbation and the wave strength are sufficiently small. In this paper, we introduce two auxiliary functions and reformulate our problem into two perturbation problems adapted to the structure of the system. This enables us to prove a result analogous to those obtained in previous studies, without assuming the differentiability of $b(t)$. The auxiliary functions are given by the differential equations $1+g'(t)=b(t)g(t)$ and $1-h'(t)=b(t)h(t)$, respectively. Our result shows that it suffices to assume $b\in C([0,\infty))$, $b(t)\asymp(1+t)^{-λ}$, and $|g'(t)|\lesssim(1+t)^{-(1-λ)}$ to obtain convergence to a diffusion wave.

☆ The compressible-incompressible CAO problem introduced by Lions, Temam and Wang
Tarek Zöchling
We study the (CAO) system of Lions-Temam-Wang, describing a compressible atmosphere coupled to an incompressible ocean through a fully nonlinear boundary condition representing wind stress at the interface. In their foundational work, the system is reformulated in pressure coordinates under the assumption that the pressure is constant at the interface, leading to a purely incompressible system. In this article, we prove for the first time the strong well-posedness of the coupled compressible-incompressible system both locally and globally for small initial data.

☆ Global-in-Time Nonrelativistic Limit and KAM Tori for the Complex Klein-Gordon Equation on the Circle
Andrea Belloni
This paper establishes a global-in-time nonrelativistic limit for families of small-amplitude quasi-periodic solutions of the cubic complex Klein-Gordon equation on the circle. Firstly, we construct by a KAM block scheme, small-amplitude two-frequency invariant tori and show that their linear stability depends on whether the two excited Fourier indices coincide or are distinct: coincident indices yield linearly stable tori, whereas distinct indices yield partially hyperbolic tori. Moreover, controlling the dependence of the KAM scheme on the speed of light, we construct quasi-periodic solutions whose frequencies, after a gauge transformation, coincide exactly with those of quasi-periodic solutions of the limiting coupled NLS system, obtaining an approximation uniform for all times in the nonrelativistic regime. By this result, we further show that there exists a positive-measure set of frequencies such that, for each frequency, we can fix a quasi-periodic solution of the coupled NLS system and a suitable subsequence of Klein-Gordon solutions converging globally in time to the fixed NLS solution.
☆ Global well-posedness for the 2D full compressible viscous non-resistive magnetohydrodynamic system
Liening Qiao, Juntao Sun, Jiahong Wu, Fuyi Xu
This paper establishes the global well-posedness and nonlinear stability of the 2D full compressible viscous non-resistive magnetohydrodynamic system $\mathbb T^2$, for smooth initial data close to the equilibrium with constant density and temperature, zero velocity and background magnetic field $\mathbf e_2=(0,1)$. Neither the density nor the magnetic field is damped or diffused in this system. Here, we impose no Diophantine condition on the background magnetic field, no symmetry on the data and no special geometry on the domain. Our proof rests on two intrinsic stabilizing mechanisms hidden in the structure of the system. First, the background magnetic field generates damped wave structures which provide dissipation for the $x_2$-derivatives of the density and of the magnetic field. Second, we introduce a new good unknown $Φ$, an effective total pressure gradient that combines the density, the temperature with the magnetic pressure. Although none of its constituents is dissipative by itself, we show that the coupling of $Φ$ with the divergence of the velocity and with the temperature produces dissipation for $Φ$ in all directions, together with an extra regularization of the divergence of the velocity. Combining these two mechanisms with new anisotropic commutator estimates and a hierarchy of time-weighted energy estimates, we prove that the system admits a unique global solution in $H^N(\mathbb T^2)$ for every $N\geq5$, and obtain a uniform-in-time bound on the highest-order energy as well as explicit algebraic decay rates. Even in comparison with the known result for the simpler isentropic counterpart, where the highest-order energy was only shown to grow at most algebraically in time for data in $H^{N}$ with $N\geq10$, our result removes the possible growth and lowers the regularity requirement to $N\geq5$.
☆ A Sharp Nodal Measure Bound for the Mixed Clamped--Navier Biharmonic Eigenvalue Problem in Dimensions $n\ge 2$
Hairong Liu, Long Tian
We estimate the interior nodal set of real eigenfunctions of $Δ^2u=λu$ on a bounded connected Euclidean domain. Each boundary component is either of class $C^\infty$ with clamped conditions or of class $C^{2,α}$ and subject to Navier conditions. We obtain $\mathcal H^{n-1}(\{u=0\}\capΩ)\le C_Ωλ^{1/4}$ for $n\ge2$. A spectral inequality on auxiliary clamped collars supplies fixed-scale interior mass. On clamped patches we localize the Carleman estimates of Liu, Tian and Yang. On Navier patches a single harmonic function with trace $u$ controls the two boundary data required for subdivision at every spatial scale. Summing an index linear in local doubling and frequency gives the stated bound. An annulus with one component of each type realizes its order of growth.
☆ Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya inequalities on the lattice graph \(\mathbb Z^N\)
Chao Ji, Kai Sheng
In this paper, we study the following Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya inequality on the lattice graph \(\mathbb Z^N\): \[ \sum_{j=1}^N\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z^N}|u(z)-u(z-e_j)|^2 -C_H(n,m)\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z^N\setminusΣ} \frac{|u(z)|^2}{d_Σ(z)^2} \geq\overlineκ_{m,n}\|u\|_{\ell^{2^*}(\mathbb Z^N)}^2, \quad u\in C_c(\mathbb Z^N\setminusΣ), \] where \(n,m\geq1\), \(N=n+m\geq3\), \(Σ=\mathbb Z^n\times\{0\}\), \(2^*=2N/(N-2)\), \(e_j\) is the \(j\)-th coordinate vector, \(d_Σ(z):=\inf_{ζ\inΣ}|z-ζ|\), and \(C_H(n,m)\) is the best constant for the Hardy inequality on \(\mathbb Z^N\setminusΣ\). Using the supersolution method and multilinear interpolation, we first prove that the best constant \(\overlineκ_{m,n}\) is positive if and only if either \(1\leq m\leq8\) and \(n\geq1\), or \(m=9\) and \(n\geq14\). Then, we show that \[ \overlineκ_{m,n}=\overline S_N \quad\text{if }m=2\text{ or }(m,n)=(1,2), \] where \(\overline S_N\) is the best constant in the critical Sobolev inequality on \(D^{1,2}(\mathbb Z^N)\). Moreover, for \(m\neq2\) and \(N\geq4\), we prove \(0\leq\overlineκ_{m,n}<\overline S_N\). Finally, using the equality \(\overlineκ_{2,n}=\overline S_{n+2}\), we prove that \(\overlineκ_{2,n}\) is not attained, while for \((m,n)=(1,2)\), we establish nonattainment of \(\overlineκ_{1,2}\) by developing a duality argument based on a comparison of Green functions.

☆ Propagation of chaos with singular potentials: A weighted duality approach
Phan Thành Nam, Toan T. Nguyen
We establish the propagation of chaos and derive the Vlasov equation from a many-body $N$-particle system in the mean-field regime with singular interaction forces bounded by $|x|^{-α-1}$ for $0\le α<(d-1)/2$ in dimensions $d\ge 2$, which in particular include the full range of sub-Coulomb interactions in three dimensions as well as the Coulomb interaction in two dimensions. Our proof is based on an energy-based framework for deriving weighted uniform bounds on cumulants that builds upon the recent duality method developed by Bresch--Duerinckx--Jabin in combination with a new Morawetz-type estimate, allowing us to remove the restriction to locally square-integrable interaction force kernels and handle more singular regimes.

☆ Large-scale regularity theory for optimal $p-$transport maps and application to concentration in the matching problem
Michael Goldman, Lukas Koch, Dario Trevisan
We consider the random bipartite matching problem between two independent families of uniformly distributed points in dimension three and higher, for the cost given by the $p$-th power of the distance. We show that, up to logarithmic factors, every moment of the displacement of the optimal matching is of the order of the typical interparticle distance. This is a higher integrability, or Calderón--Zygmund type, estimate for optimal transport, and it settles, on the torus and up to logarithmic factors, a recent conjecture of D'Achille, Mattesini and the third author. As a consequence, we obtain concentration of the matching cost around its mean for every $p\ge2$. The proof combines a deterministic large-scale regularity theory for optimal transport with $p$-costs, based on a harmonic approximation by a non-linear elliptic equation of $p$-Laplacian type, with tail bounds on local matching costs.
☆ Nonlinear stability of viscous shock waves for the one--dimensional Navier--Stokes equations with singular viscosity
Guanghan Zhao, Jingyu Li, Xiaowen Li, Changchun Liu, Ming Mei
We study the nonlinear stability of viscous shock waves for the one--dimensional isentropic Navier--Stokes system with fast diffusion and singular viscosity. The waves connect a positive left state to zero specific volume at the right far field, where the density becomes unbounded and the viscous coefficient is singular. Under a vanishing--stress condition, we first establish the existence and uniqueness, up to a shift, of a monotone profile with an algebraic right tail. We then prove global existence and convergence to the profile for sufficiently small perturbations in weighted Sobolev spaces. The main difficulties stem from the singular nonlinear viscous term. We note that the existing approach for treating scalar conservation law with singular viscosity can not be applied to Navier--Stokes equations. We propose some new technique: after introducing an effective velocity and using an anti--derivative method, we establish unusual interactive--energy--estimates and thereby the expected energy estimates for velocity by coupling the two perturbation equations; furthermore, we introduce an auxiliary functional to eliminate uncontrollable terms. The artful weighted--energy estimates play a crucial role for treating singularity.

☆ Infinitely Many Plasma Echo Cascades and Sobolev Norm Divergence at the Gevrey-3 Threshold
Yue Luo
We construct a global solution to the confined Vlasov--Poisson system near a fixed homogeneous Penrose-stable equilibrium that exhibits infinite-time growth driven by nonlinear plasma echoes. For every sufficiently small \(ε>0\), the initial perturbation has size \(O(ε)\) in a Gevrey-3 norm with radius \(λ_0\simeqε^{1/3}\). The corresponding solution is real and neutral, and the full distribution remains nonnegative. Its kinetic profile scatters in a lower Sobolev topology, while the spatial density and electric field decay. Nevertheless, the kinetic profile satisfies \[ \lim_{t\to\infty}\|f(t)\|_{H^{1000}_{z,v}}=\infty. \] The construction combines infinitely many well-separated echo cascades within a single global nonlinear solution. Each cascade generates a high-frequency output that persists under the subsequent evolution, and the accumulated outputs produce divergence in a fixed Sobolev norm. Thus, unlike finite-time echo amplification, the instability persists to arbitrarily large times despite scattering and macroscopic Landau damping. The construction identifies an instability mechanism at the critical amplitude-dependent Gevrey-3 radius \(λ_0\simeqε^{1/3}\), where cumulative echo amplification balances the initial Fourier decay.
☆ When and why can integral constraints improve the accuracy of physics-informed neural networks?
Myeong-Su Lee
Adding constraints obtained by integrating governing equations to the loss has been reported to improve the accuracy of physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) in several applications, but mathematical understanding of these benefits remains limited. For several partial differential equations (PDEs), we derive stability estimates for losses with and without integral constraints. The comparison reveals that in certain parameter regimes, the standard loss has very weak control over specific error components, and that the integral constraints restore uniform control of these components. This explains when and why the constraints improve accuracy. Finally, numerical experiments support this interpretation. In parameter regimes where the standard loss is predicted to have weak control over those components, the two losses indeed show clear differences in accuracy. Conversely, in regimes where the standard loss retains sufficient control, both losses yield similar accuracy.
☆ Separated solutions for a critical competitive system with sublinear coupling in domains with shrinking holes
Zijuan Gao, Qing Guo, Chengxiang Zhang
We construct nonnegative, fully nontrivial separated solutions for the critical competitive system of two coupled elliptic equations with a sublinear competitive coupling, in a bounded domain with two shrinking holes, for $N\ge5$ and every fixed $β<0$; each component concentrates at one of the holes and vanishes near the other. The coupling is not $C^1$ at the origin, so a direct Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction is unavailable, and the reduction has to be closed in a Lebesgue space although the matching requires $L^\infty$ control. We therefore solve a nonlinear outer problem by minimization, derive the dead-core property, solve the two scalar inner problems by a nonlinear contraction, match the inner and outer solutions, and close the scale and position equations by a Brouwer degree argument. This gives a Coron-type construction in the high-dimensional sublinear-coupling regime.
☆ Blow-up suppression for the Patlak--Keller--Segel--Navier--Stokes system by Taylor--Couette flow outside a disk
Lili Wang
Taylor--Couette devices have been investigated for enzymatic reactions and cell culture, where cylinder rotation provides a means of controlling mixing and mass transfer (Schrimpf et al., AIChE J., 2021). Motivated by these applications, this paper studies blow-up suppression in the two-dimensional Patlak--Keller--Segel--Navier--Stokes system outside the unit disk. We prove that sufficiently strong Taylor--Couette flow yields a unique global strong solution whose density and concentration are uniformly bounded in time, without smallness assumptions on the initial cell mass or the fixed initial velocity perturbation. The main difficulty is that the angular shear tends to zero at infinity, so decay estimates on bounded regions do not directly control the full solution. To overcome this difficulty, radially weighted energy estimates exploit the radial velocity to control the density and vorticity at large radii. Combining these bounds with linear decay estimates and an energy comparison with the radial chemotaxis solution yields convergence of the density in $L^2$ to the radial solution with angularly averaged initial density, uniformly on fixed finite time intervals away from $t=0$ as the rotation amplitude tends to infinity. The decay of the radial solution then makes the full density small in $L^2$ at a finite time. An energy estimate preserves this smallness and gives global continuation.
☆ A Uniform Positive Lower Bound for the Analyticity Radius of KdV on the Real Line
Ming Wang, Jie Zeng
We show that, for the Korteweg--de Vries equation on the real line with real-valued initial data in an $L^2$-based analytic class, the radius of spatial analyticity of the solution has a fixed positive lower bound for all time. This improves the previous quantitative lower bounds, which tend to zero as $|t|\to\infty$. The proof uses a positive measure representation of the Hamiltonian multipliers to sum the KdV Hamiltonians into an exactly conserved energy that controls the analytic norm.
☆ Stability analysis and critical thresholds in a nonlocal advection diffusion model of wound healing on bounded domains
Ilyas Mustapha, Mikayla Gregory
Nonlocal advection diffusion models describe how wound healing depends on the strength of cell-cell adhesion and the cell sensing radius. Depending on these parameters, the wound may close completely or remain in a persistent state with a spatially nonuniform cell density. The model combines random cell movement, cell proliferation, and cell-cell adhesion within a finite sensing radius. We first derive the dispersion relation on the whole line and use it to compute the critical sensing radius and the corresponding wavelength. This relation shows that diffusion and cell proliferation stabilize the healed state, while cell-cell adhesion can make it unstable. On a bounded interval, the cell density is fixed at the healthy value on an exterior collar. In this setting, we establish conditions that keep the cell density within a positive bounded range, derive a sufficient condition for nonlinear exponential stability that depends on domain size, and formulate and numerically solve the associated linear spectral problem. The analysis shows how reducing the domain size can stabilize the healed state at parameter values for which the whole line model is linearly unstable. Finally, we compute critical sensing radii and domain sizes numerically and compare the sufficient stability bounds with the transitions observed in wound simulations involving perturbations of finite amplitude.
☆ On the regularity of stationary solutions to free boundary problems
Daniel Restrepo
In this note, we improve the regularity of Hölder continuous stationary solutions with respect to inner variations which are harmonic outside their zero set. We obtain a $\sqrt{\log}$-Lipschitz estimate for a class of solutions allowing a generalized phase variable and including the two-phase problem. In the case of the one-phase problem, we can improve to Lipschitz regularity. In particular, we show that the initial Lipschitz assumption in the class of variational solutions considered by Kriventsov and Weiss can be replaced by any positive Hölder exponent

♻ ☆ Finite-difference least square methods for solving Hamilton-Jacobi equations using neural networks
Carlos Esteve-Yagüe, Richard Tsai, Alex Massucco
We present a simple algorithm to approximate the viscosity solution of Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) equations by means of an artificial deep neural network. The algorithm uses a stochastic gradient descent-based method to minimize the least square principle defined by a monotone, consistent numerical scheme. We analyze the least square principle's critical points and derive conditions that guarantee that any critical point approximates the sought viscosity solution. The use of a deep artificial neural network on a finite difference scheme lifts the restriction of conventional finite difference methods that rely on computing functions on a fixed grid. This feature makes it possible to solve HJ equations posed in higher dimensions where conventional methods are infeasible. We demonstrate the efficacy of our algorithm through numerical studies on various canonical HJ equations across different dimensions, showcasing its potential and versatility.
comment: 34 pages, 11 figures, 4 tables
♻ ☆ Geometric Properties of positive solutions of Lane-Emden problems on convex domains of $§^2$
Massimo Grossi, Luigi Provenzano, Daniel Raom
We study positive solutions of the Dirichlet problem $-Δu = u^p$ in a uniformly convex domain $Ω\subset §^2$, $u= 0$ on $\partialΩ.$ For $p=1$, we assume that the right-hand side is replaced by $λ_1 u$, where $λ_1$ is the first eigenvalue of $-Δ$ on $Ω$ with zero Dirichlet boundary condition. We prove that for $0 \leq p < 1$ the unique positive solution $u$ is such that $u^{\frac{1-p}{2}}$ is strictly concave in $Ω$, while for $1 < p \leq 3$ every positive solution $u$ which belongs to the connected component of the least-energy branch of solutions issued from $p=1$ is such that $u^{\frac{1-p}{2}}$ is strictly convex in $Ω$.
♻ ☆ Self-similarity and diffusive limits for linear kinetic equations: a Wild sum approach
José A. Cañizo, Stéphane Mischler, Niccolò Tassi
We prove that linear collisional kinetic equations in the whole space without confinement mechanism display a long-time self-similar behaviour. This drastically improves the recently known results (decay estimates) about the solutions in such a context, providing the first result regarding this self-similar behaviour. As a consequence, we also establish a uniform-in-time convergence of the suitably rescaled solutions to their diffusion limit, which is also new. The class of equations considered includes some BGK type equations, some kinetic nonlocal Fokker--Planck-type equations and some kinetic (possibly fractional) Fokker--Planck equations, for which we are able to write explicitly solutions through a Wild sum (or Dyson series) or we can manage some accurate computations on the Fourier side.

♻ ☆ Interior $C^2$ Estimates and a Liouville Theorem for the Complex Monge-Ampère Equation under a Quadratic Lower Bound
Jingchen Hu, Li Sheng
Let $n\ge2$ and let $u$ be a locally bounded plurisubharmonic Bedford-Taylor solution of the complex Monge-Ampère equation $\det(u_{i\bar j})=f$. Assume that in a sufficiently large ball centered at the origin in $\mathbb{C}^{n}$ \[ u(z)\ge δ\sum_{i=1}^{n}|x_i|^2,\qquad x_i=\operatorname{Re}z_{i},\qquad δ>0, \] and $u(0)\leq H$. If $f$ is Dini-continuous, bounded above and bounded away from zero, and satisfies $Δ_{\mathbb {R}}(f^{1/n})\ge-K$ in distributions, we derive an interior bound for the real $C^{2}$ norm on the unit ball $B_{1}(0)$. When $f\equiv1$, every entire solution satisfying $u(z)\geδ\sum_{i=1}^{n}|\operatorname{Re}z_i|^2$ for all $z\in\mathbb{C}^{n}$ and some $δ>0$ is a real quadratic polynomial.
♻ ☆ Regularity and Decay for Navier-Slip Fluid-Structure Interaction in Exterior Domains
Buma Jin Jin
We study the linearized motion of a spherical rigid body immersed in an incompressible viscous fluid occupying the whole space, under Navier slip boundary conditions with friction. While semigroup regularity and decay estimates are well understood for the no-slip case, such results have been limited to bounded domains in the slip setting. By exploiting the geometric regularity of the sphere, we establish strong $L^q$-regularity, bounded analyticity, and sharp $ L^q-L^r$ estimates for the corresponding fluid-structure operator. These results would provide a foundation for constructing strong $W^{2,1}_q$ solutions and Kato-type solutions to the corresponding nonlinear system.
♻ ☆ On the two critical exponents for a dispersive equation with weak dissipation
Marcello D'Abbicco, Antonio Lagioia
In this paper, we study a nonlinear Cauchy problem written in normal form \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} u_{tt} + A u+ Bu_t =D|u|^α, & t\geq 0, x \in \mathbb{R}^n\\ u(0,x)=u_0(x),\,u_t(0,x)=u_1(x). \end{cases} \end{equation*} Here~ $Af=\mathscr{F}^{-1}(a(ξ)^2\mathscr{F}f)$, with $a(ξ)$ homogeneous of order $k > 0$ under the assumption that the Hessian matrix of $a(ξ)$ is nonsingular, the operator $Bf=\mathscr{F}^{-1}(b(ξ)\mathscr{F}f)$ represents a weak dissipation, in the sense that $b(ξ) \sim 1$ as $|ξ| \to \infty$ and %, in several models, $D=B$ but we also consider the case $Df=ν\ast (-Δ)^δ(I-Δ)^{-δ}$, with $ν$ a bounded measure and $δ\geq k/2$. We derive $L^p-L^q$ estimates of the linear solution operator to the considered model and we prove the transition from a Fujita-type exponent to a Strauss-type exponent for the global-in-time existence of small data solution for the corresponding nonlinear problems.
comment: This is the final version of the paper, accepted for publication in Annali dell'Università di Ferrara
♻ ☆ Local Smoothing Estimates of a Class of Schrödinger Operators on Waveguides Using Refined Decoupling
Wenchang Sun, Jiheng Tan
We prove local smoothing estimates for a class of Schrödinger operators on waveguides. Our results extend the previously known range of exponents in every dimension and are sharp in certain cases. The proof develops a transference argument that preserves the discrete periodic frequency structure, together with a refined decoupling estimate adapted to waveguides. We also derive consequences for Euclidean local smoothing and almost everywhere convergence.
comment: 66 Pages
♻ ☆ Equi-integrable approximation of Sobolev mappings between manifolds
Jean Van Schaftingen
We show that limits of sequences of smooth maps between compact Riemannian manifolds with equi-integrable $W^{1, p}$-Sobolev energy can always be strongly approximated by smooth maps, giving a counterpart of Hang's density result in $W^{1, 1}$ for the Sobolev space $W^{1, p}$ with integer $p \ge 2$. Our result extends to higher-order Sobolev spaces and is straightforward in fractional Sobolev spaces. We also provide a proof based on the weak continuity of Jacobians in the cases where the cohomological criterion of Bethuel, Demengel, Colon and Hélein applies.

♻ ☆ Global-in-time L p -- L q estimates for solutions of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck equation
Xue Ping Wang, Lu Zhu
In this work, we prove an optimal global-in-time $L^p \to L^q$ estimate for solutions to the Kramers-Fokker-Planck equation with short range potential in dimension three. Our result shows that the decay rate as t $\rightarrow$ +$\infty$ is the same as the heat equation in x-variables and the divergence rate as t $\rightarrow$ 0 + is related to the sub-ellipticity with loss of 1/3 derivatives of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck operator.
♻ ☆ Refined Strichartz Estimates for sub-Laplacians in Heisenberg and $H$-type groups
Davide Barilari, Steven Flynn
We obtain refined Strichartz estimates for the sub-Riemannian Schrödinger equation on $H$-type Carnot groups using Fourier restriction techniques. In particular, we extend the previously known Strichartz estimates previously obtained for the Heisenberg group also to non radial initial data. The same arguments permits to obtain refined Strichartz estimates for the wave equation on $H$-type groups. Our proof is based on estimates for the spectral projectors for sub-Laplacians and reinterprets Strichartz estimates as Fourier restriction theorems for nilpotent groups in the context of trace-class operator valued measures.

♻ ☆ A Sharp Planar Fractional Isoperimetric Inequality
Xiaosheng Lin, Dachun Yang, Sibei Yang, Wen Yuan, Yangyang Zhang
In this article, we prove the sharp form of the fractional isoperimetric inequality in the plane, originally posed by Maz'ya [Problem 1, Integral Equations Operator Theory, 2018]. More precisely, we show that, for any given $s\in(0,1)$ and any bounded domain $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ with $C^1$ boundary, $$ P_s(Ω) \le \frac{π^{s-\frac{1}{2}}Γ\left(\frac{3-s}{2}\right)}{s(1-s)Γ\left(\frac{4-s}{2}\right)}\left[\mathcal{H}^1(\partialΩ)\right]^{2-s}, $$ where $P_s$ denotes the fractional $s$-perimeter, $Γ$ denotes the Gamma function, and $\mathcal{H}^{1}$ denotes the $1$-dimensional Hausdorff measure on $\mathbb{R}^2$. The constant is sharp and equality is attained by the disk. The proof proceeds in three steps: reducing the fractional perimeter to a chord functional, reducing connected domains to convex bodies, and proving the sharp convex chord inequality via a fractional Willmore-type inequality, a variational formula along outer parallel bodies, and asymptotic analysis.

♻ ☆ An inverse problem for semilinear elliptic equations with generalized Kerr-type nonlinearities
Pu-Zhao Kow, Rulin Kuan
We study the inverse problem of reconstructing the convex hull of unknown inclusions in semilinear elliptic equations with nonanalytic nonlinearities, by extending Ikehata's enclosure method to accommodate such nonlinear effects. To overcome the lack of the higher-order differentiability required for the Taylor-based construction, we construct an approximate solution based on the linearized equation through a first-iteration approximation. Under suitable structural conditions on the nonlinearity, we establish a reconstruction result for the convex hull of the inclusion. The method applies to a broad class of generalized Kerr-type nonlinearities that need not be analytic, without requiring an explicit formula for the nonlinear term. We also address the numerical challenges arising from the exponential decay of the CGO test data and show how they limit the accuracy of an implementation in double-precision arithmetic.

♻ ☆ The Dirichlet problem for sum Hessian equations on uniformly $(k-1)$-convex domains
Changyu Ren, Ziyi Wang
In this paper, we mainly study the sum Hessian equation with general boundary values in the case $2\leq k\leq n$. Under the conditions that the boundary is uniformly $(k-1)$-convex, the right-hand side is monotone non-decreasing in $u$, convex in the gradient, and has a suitably small linear gradient growth, we prove the existence of a unique smooth admissible solution. The proof constructs the global subsolution and gradient barriers by using strictly $k$-convex function, and derives the boundary second-order estimates from the tangential linearizations and a duality inequality for the boundary curvature.

♻ ☆ Entropic metastability for drifted reflected Brownian motion: quasi-stationary distributions, regularity, and the exit position distribution
Louis Carillo, Lo{ï}s Delande, Boris Nectoux
Motivated by entropic metastability and the narrow escape problem, we investigate quasi-stationary distributions for reflected, drifted elliptic diffusions under mixed absorbing-reflecting boundary conditions on a bounded domain. We address two problems, which are solved completely independently of each other. First, using purely probabilistic tools, we prove the existence and uniqueness of a quasi-stationary distribution under minimal regularity assumptions on the coefficients (the case of an unbounded domain is also analyzed). Second, using spectral theory and the theory of strongly continuous semigroups on L p spaces, we study the analytical properties of the quasistationary distribution. We relate it to the principal eigenfunction of the adjoint of the associated (non-symmetric) infinitesimal generator with mixed absorbing-reflecting boundary conditions, and we establish its regularity up to the interface between the two boundary parts. We also fully characterize the law of the exit point when the process is initially distributed according to its quasistationary distribution. In particular, we work on domains in which the absorbing (Dirichlet) and reflecting (Neumann) parts of the boundary meet tangentially, without forming any non-trivial angle, a configuration that raises genuine regularity difficulties for the solutions of the associated mixed boundary value problem.
♻ ☆ Low regularity potentials in heterogeneous Cahn--Hilliard functionals
Riccardo Cristoferi, Jakob Deutsch, Luca Pignatelli
In this paper, we study the prototypical model of liquid-liquid phase separation, the Cahn-Hilliard functional, in a highly irregular setting. Specifically, we analyze potentials with low regularity vanishing on space-dependent wells. Under remarkably weak hypotheses, we establish a robust compactness result. Strengthening the regularity of the wells and of the growth of the potential close to the wells only slightly, we completely characterize the asymptotic behavior of the associated family of functionals through a $Γ$-convergence analysis. As a notable technical result, we prove the existence of geodesics for a degenerate metric and establish a uniform bound on their Euclidean length.
♻ ☆ Higher-order estimates for $p$-harmonic functions in the plane
Juan J. Manfredi, Aelson Sobral, Eduardo V. Teixeira, José Miguel Urbano
Closing a longstanding gap in the theory, we establish uniform interior $C^{k,β}$ estimates for planar $p$-harmonic functions with $12$.

♻ ☆ A Study of the PDE Model for the Anisotropic Consensus-Based Optimization
Keyu Li, Hui Huang
We investigate the nonlinear Fokker--Planck equation associated with anisotropic consensus-based optimization. Under suitable assumptions on the objective function, we establish global existence and uniqueness of density valued weak solutions for bounded initial probability densities with finite fourth moment. The main analytical challenge arises from the component-wise degeneracy of the diffusion, which vanishes along moving coordinate hyperplanes determined by the weighted consensus point. To overcome this difficulty, we develop spatial translation estimates based on weighted gradient bounds and uniform density estimates. Combined with temporal translation and moment estimates, these yield strong compactness in $L^2((0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^d)$ through the Fréchet--Kolmogorov compactness criterion, enabling passage to the limit in the regularized equations. Uniqueness is established through the associated McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equation and Wasserstein stability of the weighted consensus point. Furthermore, we prove the propagation of $H^2$-regularity for sufficiently regular initial data.

♻ ☆ Abstract Formulation of Mean-Field Models and Propagation of Chaos
Tau Shean Lim, Chao Dun Teoh
We formulate a unified abstract framework for mean-field particle systems and their macroscopic limits from the perspective of differential equations and functional analysis. Combining semigroup theory with optimal transport, we study measure-valued evolutions directly through their generators, allowing different classes of mean-field models to be treated within a common structure. Specifically, the framework involves (1) formulating mean-field models abstractly using semigroups and generators; (2) establishing well-posedness of the corresponding nonlinear mean-field evolution equations in a class of solutions stable under approximation; and (3) proving quantitative propagation of chaos for the associated $N$-particle systems. The central tool is the transport derivative, which measures the infinitesimal variation of transport costs between Markov evolutions. We establish transport-stability criteria expressed through local generator inequalities and show how these criteria underpin both nonlinear well-posedness and particle approximation. When the generator's dependence on the law is controlled by averaged Hilbert-valued features, we obtain an $O(N^{-1})$ sampling contribution to the quadratic Wasserstein estimate through a variance argument. As an application, we obtain quantitative propagation of chaos for Lévy-type mean-field systems with state- and law-dependent drift, diffusion, and jump kernels under intrinsic transport conditions. The admissible jump kernels extend beyond those generated by multiplicative Lévy noise, demonstrating the scope of the abstract framework.

We give new proofs of interior second derivative estimates for the quadratic Hessian and Monge-Ampère equations with Dini continuous right-hand sides. For the Monge-Ampère equation, the proof is localised on sublevel sets of a strictly convex solution.

This type of NLEP appears frequently in pattern formation in reaction-diffusion systems. We show that on the even subspace, strict spectral stability holds exactly for $\Reγ>1$ when $r=(p+3)/2$. In the $γ$-plane, when $r>(p+3)/2$, two conjugate boundary arcs open to the left from $γ=1$, and the strictly stable region lies to their right. When $r<(p+3)/2$, the arcs open to the right, and the strictly stable region lies between them. ♻ ☆ Geometric bounds for Steklov and weighted Neumann eigenvalues on Euclidean domains
Denis Vinokurov
We obtain sharp upper bounds for the first two nonzero Steklov eigenvalues among bounded domains in Euclidean spaces of dimension $d \geq 7$ under a natural normalization involving volume and boundary measure. We further establish strict upper bounds with sharp constants for all higher Steklov eigenvalues on simply connected planar domains with continuous boundary and finite boundary length. Beyond the second nonzero eigenvalue, these bounds were previously known only for smooth planar domains.

In this paper, we study the multiplicity of positive normalized solutions for the following Schrödinger equation with nonlinear point defects on a general metric graph $\G=(\V,\E)$, possibly with infinitely many edges \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} u'' = λu & \text{on every } \e \in \E, \\ \int_\G \abs{u}^2\, dx = μ& \\ \displaystyle \sum_{\e \succ \vv} u'_\e(\vv) = -\abs{u(\vv)}^{p-2}u(\vv) & \text{at every } \vv \in \V_0, \\ \displaystyle \sum_{\e \succ \vv} u'_\e(\vv) = 0 & \text{at every } \vv \in \V \setminus \V_0, \end{cases} \end{equation*} where $p>2$, $\G$ is connected, $\V_0 \subset \V$ is nonempty, $μ>0$ is a given constant, $λ$ is an unknown Lagrange multiplie. For $p\neq4$, every fixed nonempty finite set $W\subset\V_0$ gives at least $2^{\#W}-1$ distinct positive normalized solutions, for every sufficiently small mass $μ>0$ if $p>4$ and for every sufficiently large mass $μ>0$ if $20$ if $p>4$, and at every sufficiently large mass $μ>0$ if $20$ if $20$ if $p>4$. In the $L^2$-critical ($p=4$) case, under local conditions near the selected defect vertices, analogous results hold for masses slightly below $kq^2/2$, where $k$ is the number of these vertices and $q$ is their common degree.

☆ Conditionally Euclidean distance matrices
Shivani Goel, Hiroshi Kurata
We introduce a new class of matrices called conditional Euclidean distance matrices in this paper. These matrices are a generalisation of Euclidean distance matrices. We develop the theory of conditional Euclidean distance matrices and show that these matrices represent the squared Lorentzian distance between points of a Minkowski space. We also highlight the connection of conditional Euclidean distance matrices with the representation of hierarchical data in machine learning and the theory of general relativity in physics.
☆ A constructive inverse for the Jordan-von Neuman operator on abelian groups
Dorian Popa, Mircea Dan Rus
For an abelian group $G$ and a real Banach space $X$, we study the inhomogeneous Jordan--von Neumann equation $\mathsf{Q}[f] = g$, where $\mathsf{Q}$ is the quadratic difference operator of the parallelogram law. We characterize the functions $g$ in the image of $\mathsf{Q}$ and, under a summability hypothesis, recover a solution explicitly by an iteration on the diagonal followed by a propagation argument; neither regularity of $g$ nor divisibility of $G$ is required. As a consequence we obtain a sharp stability estimate of Forti--Găvruţa type for the quadratic functional equation.
comment: 19 pages
☆ Perturbed, suprametric, and interpolative contractions are metric contractions
Firuz Kamalov
We show that the fixed point theory of perturbed metric spaces, b-suprametric spaces, and interpolative metric spaces reduces to the metric case. A mapping is a perturbed contraction with constant $λ$ if and only if it is a Banach contraction with constant $λ$ for a metric that dominates the exact metric. Thus the theorem of Jleli and Samet is the Banach contraction principle in a finer metric, and we show that this metric cannot be chosen equivalent to the exact one. We also show that the fixed point theorem claimed for perturbed Kannan mappings is false. A b-suprametric is a logarithmic transform of a b-metric with the same constant, and an interpolative metric is a power of a metric with an explicit exponent, which is optimal for $α= 1/2$. Consequently, contractive conditions of maximum type in these spaces are equivalent to the same conditions in b-metric and metric spaces.
☆ Spectral isometries and invertibility preservers on Banach algebras
Zakariae Aznay, Fadil Chabbabi
We prove that every unital surjective complex-linear spectral isometry between complex unital semisimple Banach algebras is a Jordan isomorphism, thereby giving an affirmative answer to the spectrum-preserving form of Kaplansky's conjecture. We also characterize surjective complex-linear maps between arbitrary unital Banach algebras that preserve invertibility in either direction, satisfy either spectral inclusion, or preserve the spectral radius. In particular, for a complex-linear bijection between semisimple Banach algebras, preservation of invertibility in either direction implies preservation in both directions, and either spectral inclusion implies equality of spectra, even without assuming unitality. As an application, we study preservers of the Fredholm essential spectrum and essential spectral radius.

☆ Polyanalytic $q$-Fock spaces and the polyanalytic $q$-Bargmann transform
Irfan Ali, Uwe Kähler, Michael Ruzhansky
We study polyanalytic $q$-Fock spaces from an operator-theoretic point of view. We compute the formal adjoint $A^*$ of the Jackson derivative $A=\overline{R}_{q}$ on the polynomials in $z,\overline{z}$ inside $L^{2}(\mathbb{C},μ_{q})$ and we show that, up to unimodular factors, a twist by the grading operator is the only modification of $A$ diagonal in the grading for which a deformed canonical relation $aa^*-λa^*a=I$ holds. The resulting second-order $q$-difference operator $a^*a$ is essentially self-adjoint on the polynomials and $q$-complex Hermite polynomials span its eigenspaces. These eigenspaces give the orthogonal decomposition of $L^{2}(\mathbb{C},μ_{q})$ into true polyanalytic $q$-Fock spaces. We determine the disk on which each of them is a reproducing kernel Hilbert space and we factor the corresponding unitary $q$-Bargmann transforms through powers of $a^*$.

Sanne ter Horst, Alma van der Merwe, Victor Vinnikov, Hugo J. Woerdeman
We study the single matrix point interpolation problem for positive real matrix valued functions on the right half-plane, both in the single variable setting and in the noncommutative multivariable setting. In the single variable case, a careful analysis is done for when the solution may or must have a pole at infinity. In the multivariable setting, as the pole structure at infinity can be more complicated, we focus on the case when there is no pole at infinity. The results also yield numerical algorithms for finding a solution.
☆ The rigidity phenomenon for weighted composition operators on the Fock spaces
Hong Rae Cho, Boo Rim Choe, Hyungwoon Koo, Pham Trong Tien
We establish the rigidity of canonical sums of any finite number of weighted composition operators acting from a Fock space $\mathcal{F}^p$ into another $\mathcal{F}^q$ for all possible combinations of \(p,q\in (0, \infty]\). Specifically, we show that such a sum is bounded (compact, resp.) if and only if its summands are individually bounded (compact, resp.). In the case \(p\le q\), we present two independent approaches -- one analytic and one largely algebraic -- based on some common preliminary rigidity results. As a natural byproduct of our approach, we also obtain the Reproducing Kernel Thesis.

Together with the known ordinal-sum reduction and nilpotent case, the theorem yields the same conclusion for all continuous triangular norms and, in particular, for associative bivariate copulas. It also gives a corresponding result for representable uninorms with a common neutral element.

We also show that the plain and polynomial weak topologies are distinct on bistochastic operators, confirming the distinction between the two results.

For $a,b > 0$, the conditions \[ \int_{-\infty}^\infty |f(x)| e^{ω(a|x|)} \, \mathrm{d}x < \infty \qquad \text{and} \qquad \int_{-\infty}^\infty |\widehat{f}(ξ)| e^{\varpi^*(b|ξ|)} \, \mathrm{d}ξ < \infty \] force $f = 0$ when $ab > Φ_{(ω,\varpi^*)}$, whereas the functions satisfying both conditions form a dense subspace of $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ when $ab < Φ_{(ω,\varpi^*)}$. A discrete form of the same construction yields a characterization of the nontriviality of Gelfand-Shilov spaces $\mathcal{S}^{M}_{A}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and $Σ^{M}_{A}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ in terms of their defining weight sequences $M$ and $A$, under suitable regularity assumptions.

Let $\mathscr{M}$ and $\mathscr{N}$ be non-trivial closed subspaces of a separable Hilbert space $\mathscr{H}$ such that $\mathscr{M}\cap\mathscr{N}=\{0\}$ and $\mathscr{M}+\mathscr{N}$ is dense in $\mathscr{H}$. We prove that such an operator exists if and only if $\mathscr{M}$ and $\mathscr{N}$ have a common algebraic complement. This happens if and only if either neither of the operators $(I-P)Q$ and $(I-Q)P$ is compact, or $P-Q$ is compact and $\dim(\mathscr{M}\cap\mathscr{N}^\perp)=\dim(\mathscr{M}^\perp\cap\mathscr{N})$, where $P$ and $Q$ are the orthogonal projections onto $\mathscr{M}$ and $\mathscr{N}$. Moreover, the operator can be chosen to be an involution. Consequently, the group of collineations of the diamond lattice $\{\{0\},\mathscr{M},\mathscr{N},\mathscr{H}\}$ which fix $\mathscr{M}$ and $\mathscr{N}$ is always complemented in the group of all its collineations.

☆ Operator generated topologies and the Krein property
Christian Budde, Josef Kreulich
Let $X$ be a Banach space and $Z\subseteq X^*$ a subspace separating the points of $X$. We say that $Z$ has the Krein property if the $σ(X,Z)$-closed convex hull of every norm-bounded $σ(X,Z)$-compact set is $σ(X,Z)$-compact. We show that this property passes from $Z$ to every subspace between $Z$ and its sequential weak$^*$ closure in $X^*$, and that the closed convex hulls do not change. In particular, it passes to the smallest $V^*$-invariant space $Z[V]\supseteq Z$ whenever the operator $V$ is a pointwise $σ(X,Z)$-limit of a sequence of $σ(X,Z)$-continuous operators; for nets this fails in general and holds under a double limit condition. As a source of spaces with the Krein property we show that the Mackey topologies $μ(X,Z)$ and $μ(Z,X)$ are complete if the identity of $X$ is suitably approximated by a sequence of operators whose adjoints map $X^*$ into $Z$; in particular, $μ(E^\odot,E)$ and $μ(E,E^\odot)$ are complete for every $C_0$-semigroup on a Banach space $E$ with sun dual $E^\odot$. The results are applied to the history space $\mathrm{BUC}(\mathbb{R}_{-})$ of delay equations with infinite delay, where every space of bounded measures containing $L^1(\mathbb{R}_{-})$ has the Krein property.

☆ Unbounded Gaps Between Matrix Monotonicity and Frobenius Radial Convexity

We show that the gap between matrix monotonicity and Frobenius radial convexity can be arbitrarily large. For every integer $m\ge 2$, we construct rational functions that are matrix monotone of order $m$ but not of order $m+1$, and Frobenius radially convex of order $2m-1$ but not of order $2m$. Thus, the difference between their exact matrix-monotonicity and radial-convexity orders is $m-1$, which can be arbitrarily large. As a consequence, for every $n\ge 3$, Frobenius radial convexity of order $n$ does not imply matrix monotonicity of the same order, either increasing or decreasing.

Let $H$ be a separable complex Hilbert space, and let $θ(H)$ be the class of bounded operators whose restrictions to every nonzero closed reducing subspace attain their numerical radii. We characterize this property by eigenvalues of suitable self-adjoint parts. For normal operators, membership in $θ(H)$ is equivalent to pure point spectrum and reverse well-ordering of the moduli of eigenvalues. Without normality assumptions, we prove stability under finite orthogonal direct sums using graph subspaces of closed, possibly unbounded, intertwining operators. We give a compact-perturbation criterion in terms of the essential numerical radius and show that an operator remains in $θ(H)$ under every compact perturbation if and only if it is compact. Finally, $θ(H)$ is norm-dense in $\mathcal B(H)$ and is norm closed if and only if $H$ is finite-dimensional.

This is the second part of a two-part work on semiclassical Weyl laws and Connes' integration formulas for spectral triples. It establishes three operator-theoretic results, which are used in Part I but are of independent interest. The first is a factorization formula for the fractional commutators $[|D|^{-α},a]$, which is obtained by means of double operator integrals. The second is an enhancement, for arbitrary unital spectral triples, of a lemma of Connes-Sukochev-Zanin on the differences $(a^{1/2}|D|^{-α}a^{1/2})^s-|D|^{-αs}a^s$, together with a holomorphic version of it. The third is a Tauberian theorem showing that zeta function and heat trace conditions of the type sought by Connes imply Weyl laws for the operators $aD^2a$, where $a$ ranges over positive invertible elements of the algebra. Along the way, we obtain a version for spectral triples of the Tauberian theorem of McDonald-Sukochev-Zanin without any extra regularity assumption or restriction on the degree of summability. This paper can be read largely independently of Part I.

♻ ☆ A Coarse-Geometric Interpretation of Holt's One-End Theorem
Hussain AL-Rasheed
Can a group be colored red and blue, with both color classes infinite, so that each right translation changes the color of only finitely many elements? For the group of finite subsets of the natural numbers, one can color a nonempty set by the parity of its largest element. Holt proved that no such coloring exists in an uncountable locally finite group. For the finitary coarse structure, almost invariant color classes are exactly the coarsely clopen sets; modulo finite changes, their characteristic functions give all the projections in the Higson corona algebra. We give a detailed account of Holt's coset argument in Cornulier's formulation, without using group cohomology. The argument shows why the space of coarse ends is a singleton and the full Higson corona is connected. We then show, via a separate argument for all slowly oscillating functions, that for any uncountable abelian group---in particular, an uncountable direct sum of groups of order two---Protasov's stronger conclusion holds: the full corona is a singleton.
♻ ☆ Composition operators on weighted Bergman spaces of the polydisc

We study composition operators between weighted Bergman spaces of the polydisc induced by smooth symbols. We prove a general result of continuity which only involves the behaviour of the symbol on the polytorus. We deduce from this several consequences about the automatic continuity of the induced operator. We study in depth the case of the tridisc and exhibit several examples showing that a characterization of continuity using only derivatives seems impossible.
♻ ☆ A Sharp Planar Fractional Isoperimetric Inequality
Xiaosheng Lin, Dachun Yang, Sibei Yang, Wen Yuan, Yangyang Zhang
In this article, we prove the sharp form of the fractional isoperimetric inequality in the plane, originally posed by Maz'ya [Problem 1, Integral Equations Operator Theory, 2018]. More precisely, we show that, for any given $s\in(0,1)$ and any bounded domain $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ with $C^1$ boundary, $$ P_s(Ω) \le \frac{π^{s-\frac{1}{2}}Γ\left(\frac{3-s}{2}\right)}{s(1-s)Γ\left(\frac{4-s}{2}\right)}\left[\mathcal{H}^1(\partialΩ)\right]^{2-s}, $$ where $P_s$ denotes the fractional $s$-perimeter, $Γ$ denotes the Gamma function, and $\mathcal{H}^{1}$ denotes the $1$-dimensional Hausdorff measure on $\mathbb{R}^2$. The constant is sharp and equality is attained by the disk. The proof proceeds in three steps: reducing the fractional perimeter to a chord functional, reducing connected domains to convex bodies, and proving the sharp convex chord inequality via a fractional Willmore-type inequality, a variational formula along outer parallel bodies, and asymptotic analysis.

We consider bounded Volterra-type operators $T_g$ from the weighted Bergman space $A^q_β$ to $A^p_α$. The holomorphic optimal domain $[T_{g},A^p_α]$ is introduced and shown to be a quasi-Banach space. We show that the intersection of the optimal domains is equal to $A^q_β$ if $p\le q$, while if $p>q$, it is strictly larger than $A^q_β$. Moreover, $A^q_β \subsetneq[T_{g},A^p_α]$ is established for $p\neq q$. If $p=q$, by contrast, $A^p_β$ may coincide with $[T_{g},A^p_α]$. The multiplier algebras and strict inclusions with respect to varying parameters are established. For example, we determine exactly when $[T_{g},A^s_γ] \subset [T_{g},A^p_α]$ for some $g\in \operatorname{Hol}(\mathbb{D})$. We further study the set $V_g^p$ and characterize the coincidence of the holomorphic optimal domains.

♻ ☆ Converse symplectic interlacing via low-rank singular value perturbations
Priyanka Grover, Hemant K. Mishra, Sarishti Singh, Temjensangba
The symplectic interlacing theorem states that the symplectic spectrum of a $2n \times 2n$ real symmetric positive definite matrix satisfies a $2k$-step interlacing relation with the symplectic spectrum of every $2(n-k) \times 2(n-k)$ $s$-principal submatrix. We prove the converse in this paper. More precisely, given a global symplectic spectrum of size $n$ and a local symplectic spectrum of size $n-k$ satisfying the $2k$-step interlacing inequalities, we construct a $2n \times 2n$ real symmetric positive definite matrix having the prescribed global symplectic spectrum and a $2(n-k) \times 2(n-k)$ $s$-principal submatrix of it having the prescribed local symplectic spectrum. A novelty of our method is building a connection between the $s$-principal submatrix problem and low-rank singular value perturbations. We also provide an algorithm to determine a positive definite matrix that realizes the given global and local symplectic spectra. In the context of the Gaussian quantum marginal problem, our result implies that the symplectic interlacing inequalities are not merely necessary conditions on Gaussian marginals, but are also the complete spectral compatibility conditions for the global-versus-local-mode marginal problem.

In his 1994 doctoral thesis, Bossard introduced the notion of the non-universal tree $T_{NU}(X)$ associated with each separable Banach space $X$ which does not contain an isomorphic copy of $C(2^\mathbb{N})$. Together with the order operation defined on well-founded trees, we obtain a method of classifying the complexity of separable Banach spaces by the degree of isomorphism of finite-dimensional subspaces of $C(2^\mathbb{N})$. Despite further refinement of this concept in later years, we are unaware of any specific instances of direct exhibitions of the order of the non-universal tree for a concrete space and basis. We show that if $H$ is any separable Hilbert space, then $o(T_{NU}(H)) = ω + 1$ when taken with respect to the Haar basis for $C(2^\mathbb{N})$, demonstrating that the class of Hilbert spaces is the least complex class with respect to this measurement when considering this basis.

If $E$ and $F$ are infinite dimensional Banach lattices, one of which contains a copy of $c_{0}$, then the Wittstock tensor product $E\widetilde{\otimes}_{\vert{\varepsilon}\vert}F$ contains a complemented copy of $c_{0}$. ☆ A Geometric Calderón Problem for Differential Forms
Yujun Jin, Zuoqin Wang
We establish boundary determination and global partial-data uniqueness for Karpukhin's Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator on differential $p$-forms. We derive an explicit recursion for its full symbol and determine the full boundary jet of the metric, modulo conformal gauge in the critical dimension $n=2p+2$. For $p\geq1$, partial data determine metrics that are analytic in the interior and near the measured boundary subset, up to isometry or conformal equivalence. The global uniqueness relies on a new projection-kernel embedding that detects the unobserved boundary through rank loss and small eigenvalues. We also establish global partial-data uniqueness for smooth metrics with harmonic curvature, using elliptic-transport unique continuation and, in the critical dimension, conformal-geodesic coordinates. A Weyl nondegeneracy condition further upgrades conformal equivalence to isometry.

This paper analyzes the existence and uniqueness of coexistence states for a generalized class of diffusive Lotka--Volterra predator-prey models involving spatial heterogeneities and mixed boundary conditions of non-classical type. Its main findings are the following: (a) after characterizing the existence of coexistence states, the uniqueness of the coexistence state is established, in a multidimensional context, near the curves of change of stability of the semi-trivial positive solutions of the model, (b) the one-dimensional uniqueness theorem of López-Gómez and Pardo [65,67] is sharpened up to cover the case of mixed boundary conditions of nonclassical type, (c) the multidimensional uniqueness theorem of [66] is substantially generalized up to deal with variable coefficients, and it is complemented with the global attractivity of the unique coexistence state, which excludes any Hopf bifurcation, (d) assuming Neumann boundary conditions and constant coefficients, we can sharpen, very substantially, the pioneering results of Leung [46] establishing the the constant coexistence state is the unique coexistence state of the model. In this setting, we can also prove that the constant coexistence state is a global attractor with respect to the positive solutions of the associated parabolic problem, and that it is non-degenerate, even for general differential operators, not necessarily self-adjoint. \par As this paper is a personal homage to Volterra [92] at the centenary of the publication of his foundational paper on the predator-prey model, based on the field data of D'Ancona [4], this paper begins with a review of the first scientific works in population dynamics of Vito Volterra and Umberto D'Ancona.

☆ On the $L^p$-Neumann problem for divergence form elliptic equations in the upper half-space
Mihalis Mourgoglou
A central question has been whether the $L^p$-Neumann problem is solvable for some $p\in(1,\infty)$ in the upper half-space $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}_+:=\mathbb{R}^n\times(0,\infty)$, $n\geq2$, for second-order uniformly elliptic equations in divergence form whose coefficients are either independent of the transverse variable or satisfy the Dahlberg--Kenig--Pipher (DKP) condition. We answer this question in the negative for both classes, even for matrices whose symmetric part is the identity. The two examples have the same nonzero Neumann datum $g\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n)$ of mean zero. Although $g$ is bounded and belongs to the real Hardy space $H^1(\mathbb R^n)$, neither equation admits a weak solution with this datum whose gradient has a non-tangential maximal function in $L^p(\mathbb R^n)$ for any $1\leq p<\infty$. For the variational solution $u$ associated with either matrix $A$, the non-tangential maximal functions of $\nabla_x u$, $\partial_tu$ and $(A\nabla u)_{n+1}$ each have infinite $L^p$ norm for every $1\leq p\leq\infty$. In the example with coefficients independent of the transverse variable, the equation in the interior is the Laplace equation. The matrix in the DKP example has finite $L^2$-type Carleson discrepancy from the identity. This shows that solvability of the $L^p$-Neumann problem is not stable under arbitrary Carleson perturbations of the identity. For a suitable choice of the coefficients in the lower half-space, the $L^2$ non-tangential maximal and uniform slice estimates fail for both the tangential gradient and the transverse derivative of the associated single layer potential. The $L^2$ estimate for the tangential gradient of its boundary trace also fails. We explain the role of the coefficients below the boundary and prove the $L^2$ layer potential estimates for the reflected extension when the DKP norm is sufficiently small.

Since the solutions of the original wave system are quasi-periodic in space, the main challenge is to find an appropriate function space to estimate the approximation error.

In 1880, G. Stokes [Mathematical and Physical Papers, Vol. I] studied a two-dimensional gravity water wave and conjectured that the wave crest forms a symmetric corner of angle 2pi/3 at the stagnation point. The conjecture was first proved by Amick, Fraenkel, and Toland [Acta Math. 148 (1982)] and, independently, by Plotnikov [Dinamika Sploshn. Sredy 57 (1982)] via the Nekrasov integral equation. Their proofs rely on structural assumptions, including the isolation of stagnation points and the symmetry and monotonicity of the wave profile. In 2011, Varvaruca and Weiss [Acta Math. 206 (2011)] introduced a novel geometric approach and gave a new proof of the conjecture without relying on the structural assumptions mentioned above, under a local gradient bound for the two-dimensional stream function. In this paper, we establish an optimal local gradient estimate for general variational solutions of the free boundary problem. Our approach adapts the Hopf differential method of De Philippis, Hirsch, and Nahon [arXiv:2609.12180v2] to the gravitational setting, and combines it with their abstract approximation theorem to turn the holomorphic approximation of the Hopf differential into the local gradient bounds. An important new observation is that the weighted Cauchy-Beurling correction, combined with vanishing on the lower half plane, supplies the additional height decay needed to obtain the local gradient bounds. As a consequence, we remove the a priori growth hypothesis from the geometric analysis in [Acta Math. 206 (2011)]. For general variational solutions, we establish the Stokes corner or full-density blow-up alternative. Under the stated topological and interface hypotheses, we obtain the Stokes corner and two free boundary branches that are C^1 up to the stagnation point.
