☆ Quantum Monge-Kantorovich optimal transport in spacetime through spatiotemporal Kirkwood-Dirac distributions and spatiotemporal states
Zhian Jia
Monge-Kantorovich optimal transport is a mathematical framework that determines the most efficient way to transform one probability distribution into another while minimizing a given cost function. Its central constructions include the Wasserstein distances, which quantify the space of probability distributions, and dual formulations that link to convex analysis. Its standard quantum generalization replaces probability distributions with density operators and cost function with positive semidefinite cost operator, which should be regarded as spatial quantum optimal transport. In this work, we propose the quantum optimal transport problem in spacetime through the spatiotemporal phase-space Kirkwood-Dirac quasiprobability distribution and spatiotemporal states and through spatiotemporal state. We show that the two formalisms are equivalent and related via spatiotemporal operator frames. In the Kirkwood-Dirac phase-space formalism, the spatiotemporal distribution and the cost function are complex-valued, and the spatiotemporal couplings are Kirkwood-Dirac quasiprobability distributions that yield the correct marginals for the local states. In the spatiotemporal state formalism, the cost operators are generally non-Hermitian, and the spatiotemporal couplings are generally non-Hermitian and yield the correct reduced local states. The Margenau-Hill phase-space distribution gives rise to a real-valued optimal transport in spatiotemporal phase space; in the spatiotemporal state formalism, this corresponds to a Hermitian spatiotemporal coupling state. We give a rigorous definitions and a careful discussion of its duality. We also introduce a spatiotemporal quantum Wasserstein metric based on a metric in spatiotemporal phase spaces and show that it satisfies the metric axioms.

☆ Incremental Roseland: Batch-wise Landmark Diffusion via Kernelized Sequential Karhunen--Loève Update
Jeanie Schreiber
Landmark diffusion (Roseland) computes a diffusion-map-style spectral embedding from the singular value decomposition of a degree-normalized data-to-landmark kernel matrix, at a cost far below that of full diffusion maps. It assumes, however, that all data are available at once. We introduce incremental Roseland (iRoseland), which casts the landmark affinity as a row-growing matrix whose SVD can be updated with a kernelized Sequential Karhunen--Loève (SKL) scheme. Degre correction is handled by a first order expansion about a reference mean kernel row and so that the landmark-side eigenbasis may be recovered from a single landmark-by-landmark eigendecomposition at each step. The presented method requires only a single pass over the data and runs in bounded-memory with state independent of the number of points processed. A forgetting factor lets the method track drifting distributions, and a sample-size-invariant embedding keeps outputs comparable across time. Experiments show agreement with Roseland to round-off on stationary data, and accuracy that exceeds equal-memory Roseland by an order of magnitude on long streams. On drifting data, we observe large gains from forgetting with a window matched to the drift.

En route to this we establish a Luckhaus type lemma for connections to exclude curvature concentration along blow-up sequences.

♻ ☆ Fine properties of nonlinear potentials and a unified perspective on monotonicity formulas
Luca Benatti, Alessandra Pluda, Marco Pozzetta
We rigorously show that a large family of monotone quantities along the weak inverse mean curvature flow is the limit case of the corresponding ones along the level sets of $p$-capacitary potentials. Such monotone quantities include Willmore and Minkowski-type functionals on Riemannian manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature. In $3$-dimensional manifolds with nonnegative scalar curvature, we also recover the monotonicity of the Hawking mass and its nonlinear potential theoretic counterparts. This unified view is built on a refined analysis of $p$-capacitary potentials. We prove that they strongly converge in $W^{1,q}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ as $p\to 1^+$ to the inverse mean curvature flow and their level sets are curvature varifolds. Finally, we also deduce a Gauss-Bonnet-type theorem for level sets of $p$-capacitary potentials.

The closed unit bidisc $\overline{\mathbb{D}^2}$ is known to be a spectral set for any pair $(T_1,T_2)$ of commuting contractions. When each $T_i$ is pure and has finite defect, the pair admits a much smaller spectral set: the closure of a distinguished variety $V\subset \mathbb{D}^2$. We exhibit conditions on $(T_1,T_2)$ that guarantee that no proper closed subset of $\overline{V}$ can be a spectral set. In addition, we examine the relationship between $V$ and the annihilating ideal $Ann(T_1,T_2)$ in $H^\infty(\mathbb{D}^2)$. While $V$ is typically strictly larger than the zero set of $Ann(T_1,T_2)$, we isolate a natural constrained co-extension $(S_1,S_2)$ of $(T_1,T_2)$ whose Taylor spectrum is contained in $V$ and is closely linked to the so-called support of $Ann(T_1,T_2)$. We also find simple conditions on $Ann(T_1)$ detecting whether $Ann(T_1,T_2)$ is the ideal of functions vanishing on the joint point spectrum of $(S_1^*,S_2^*)$.

Since the Pickrell diffusions that leave the Pickrell measure invariant are coherent with respect to the same projective system, we also obtain the stochastic boundary process associated with the coherent family of Pickrell diffusions.

We consider regularized Brascamp-Lieb inequalities using the theory of optimal transportation, more precisely an anisotropic version of Caffarelli's contraction theorem. The characterization of equality cases requires several new ideas to deal with difficulties, which do not appear for the non-regularized Brascamp-Lieb datum. ♻ ☆ Auxiliary Gradient-Flow Solvers for Generalized Newtonian Models
Stefano Zampini, Daniele Boffi, Gurt Dovletov, Peter Markowich
We introduce an auxiliary gradient-flow framework for variational problems with generalized Newtonian structure governed by an N-function. The key idea is to replace the nonlinear constitutive dependence on the gradient, or symmetric gradient, by an auxiliary scalar variable representing its squared magnitude. This shifts the nonlinearity from the state equation to the auxiliary variable, yielding a sequence of uniformly elliptic weighted linear problems. At the continuous level, we construct an auxiliary energy on a metric space adapted to the growth of the underlying N-function. In this topology, we prove lower semicontinuity, geodesic $λ$-convexity, and exponential convergence of the associated minimizing-movement scheme. At the finite element level, we derive a metric gradient flow through an explicit Riesz map, prove global well-posedness of the resulting semi-discrete ODE, and establish convergence to the finite element solution of the Euler--Lagrange equations of the generalized Newtonian energy. For the $p$-Laplacian and $p$-Stokes models, this gives a rigorous convergence result for $4/3\le p\le 4$, $p\ne2$, with asymptotic rate estimates beyond this range. We also propose practical time discretizations, including an operator-splitting scheme that gives the \kac iteration as a special case, and an adaptive pseudo-transient method that can be implemented using scalable linear solvers. Numerical experiments for power-law, Carreau--Yasuda, regularized Bingham, and optimal-design models demonstrate robustness, mesh-independent iteration counts in the tested regimes, and performance that matches or outperforms Newton's method.

♻ ☆ A proof of the constant-width numerical range conjecture
Muyan Jiang
We prove that the numerical range of a complex matrix has constant width \(d\) if and only if it is a closed disk of radius \(d/2\). The width in each direction is the gap between the extreme eigenvalues of a Hermitian matrix. When that gap is constant, the midpoint of the projected interval is a rational function of the direction parameter. An operator norm bound and reversal of direction then show that the midpoints are projections of a single point, the disk's center.

♻ ☆ The Operator Systems of Hankel Matrices and Complex Polynomials
Shengwei Qiu, Thomas Sinclair
Using polynomial matrix spectral factorization, we establish a complete order duality between $(n+1)\times(n+1)$ Hankel matrices and complex polynomials of degree at most $2n$ on the real line. The projection construction and trace pairing identify $e_n(t)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}t^{2j}$ as the polynomial order unit corresponding to the restriction of the matrix trace. The Cayley transform relates these matrix orders to Toeplitz matrices and truncated trigonometric polynomials, but for $n\geq 2$ the polynomial systems with units $e_n$ and $(1+t^2)^n$ are not unital order isomorphic. We establish polynomial minimality and Hankel maximality, and characterize positivity of $C^*$-algebra-valued block Hankel matrices through completely positive maps on the polynomial operator system. An augmented Vandermonde decomposition describes polynomial states as trace-one positive Hankel matrices, with extreme states given by normalized evaluations and the leading-coefficient functional at infinity.

We study $\mathcal{F}$-hypercyclicity of weighted orbits $λ_nT^nx$ for continuous linear operators $T$ on complex F-spaces, where $\mathcal{F}$ is a Furstenberg family with the cut--shift--and--paste (CuSP) property. We characterize the scalar sequences for which weighted hypercyclicity always implies ordinary hypercyclicity: their nonzero values must be bounded and bounded away from zero. This condition also guarantees weight removal for every Furstenberg family with the CuSP property. For the converse inclusion, we prove that, for any Furstenberg family $\mathcal{F}$ with the CuSP property, a bounded scalar sequence preserves all $\mathcal{F}$-hypercyclic vectors if its backward-shift $ω$-limit system is distal and does not contain the zero sequence. For chaotic operators, minimality of this system suffices. In particular, every complex nilsequence which is not identically zero preserves $\mathcal{F}$-hypercyclicity, and equality holds when its nonzero values are bounded away from zero. We also obtain simultaneous weighted return results and stability under unimodular weights with asymptotically trivial multiplicative differences.

We introduce the property of countable separation for a locally convex Hausdorff space $X$ and relate it to the existence of a metrizable coarser topology. Building on this, we demonstrate how the separability of $X$ is equivalent to the existence of a locally convex topology on the dual $X'$ that is metrizable and coarser than the weak topology $σ(X', X)$. This result generalizes known conditions for separability and provides a precise duality between separability and metrizability. We also show how to derive new and known conditions for the separability of $X$ from this characterization.

☆ Hyperbolic systems with non-diagonalisable principal part and variable multiplicities, IV: time-dependent characteristics, representation of solutions and regularity
Michael Ruzhansky, Bolys Sabitbek
We consider first-order linear hyperbolic systems with time-dependent pseudo-differential principal symbols and characteristic roots of variable multiplicity. Building on the time-independent work of Kamotski and the first author, we introduce a finite-type condition along the lifted bicharacteristic flow that accounts for the contact of time-dependent characteristic roots. Under this condition, we construct a representation of solutions using time-dependent Fourier integral operators and a Picard series whose terms become increasingly smooth. This leads to an asymptotic expansion in smoothness and local \(L^p\) regularity estimates with the expected loss of derivatives. We also apply these results to higher-order scalar weakly hyperbolic equations with involutive characteristics and time-dependent principal symbols. Finally, we consider upper triangular systems with possibly non-diagonalisable principal parts and derive a representation formula involving integrated Fourier integral operators. This extends the earlier results of Garetto, Jäh and the first author to time-dependent principal parts.
☆ Counterexamples to Grad's conjecture of any knot type
Alberto Enciso, Javier Peñafiel-Tomás, Daniel Peralta-Salas
We construct smooth magnetohydrostatic counterexamples to Grad's conjecture in toroidal domains of arbitrary knot type. The magnetic field is nonvanishing, and nested pressure tori fill the domain outside a nondegenerate magnetic axis. The equilibria have trivial Euclidean symmetry group and occur in smooth families of inequivalent configurations. On each regular pressure torus the magnetic flow is smoothly conjugate to a linear flow with any prescribed positive constant slope. A variation of this argument gives equilibria of arbitrary knot type with twist (that is, nonconstant rotational transform) and any finite regularity. A key ingredient of the proof is a deformation method that creates knot topology from axial symmetry by separating the sheets of a covering immersion into a braid, which may be useful in other deformation problems.
☆ Mean curvature flow into an ambient Riemannian manifold evolving by Ricci-Bourguignon flow
José Gomes, Matheus Hudson, Raquel Lemos
We study the mean curvature flow in Riemannian manifolds evolving by the Ricci-Bourguignon flow. Using DeTurck's trick, we establish short-time existence and uniqueness for the mean curvature flow in this time-dependent ambient geometry. In the case where the ambient metric evolves by a self-similar solution to the Ricci-Bourguignon flow, we characterize the associated mean curvature solitons and derive a Huisken monotonicity-type formula adapted to the Ricci-Bourguignon setting. As a consequence, we show that, in compact ambient manifolds, type-I singularities of the mean curvature flow in a gradient shrinking Ricci-Bourguignon soliton background have, after suitable parabolic rescaling, weighted minimal hypersurfaces as their limiting models, while in the noncompact setting, we establish the corresponding result for a gradient shrinking Schouten soliton background. This provides a geometric framework for understanding how the ambient scalar curvature influences the formation and structure of singularity models for the mean curvature flow. We also show how to construct explicit examples of mean curvature flow in a gradient Ricci-Bourguignon soliton background.

This paper is concerned with the derivation of a model governing the equilibrium configuration of two linearly elastic bodies that may come into contact with each other. The contact zone, or coincidence set, is an \emph{a priori} unknown of the model, and the equilibrium configuration is governed by variational inequalities. We introduce a new modelling paradigm in which the contact interface between the two linearly elastic bodies under consideration is now regarded as the \emph{primary variable} of an optimal control problem whose states are the unique solutions of two \emph{independent} unilateral contact problems for which this very contact interface represents the obstacle itself. As a result, the free boundary emerges as the solution of a low-dimensional optimisation problem rather than as the active set of coupled variational inequalities. We establish the existence and uniqueness of optimal controls minimising the reduced cost functional arising from the modelling paradigm introduced beforehand, and we show that the family of marginal energy functionals associated with such model $Γ$-converges to the energy functional associated with the original variational inequalities as the positive \emph{cost parameter} $β$ in the reduced cost functional tends to zero. This $Γ$-convergence argument also yields a characterisation of the coincidence set of the limit problem in terms of the optimal interfaces. We further show that, after a suitable regularisation, the reduced cost functional is Gâteaux differentiable, and that its Gâteaux derivative can be explicitly computed \emph{without solving any adjoint system}. Finally, we corroborate the $Γ$-convergence result obtained beforehand with numerical experiments on a simplified and exactly solvable configuration.

We study 2D Stokes flow in a wedge-like region bounded by a solid substrate with Navier slip and by a free surface driven by surface tension. The two meet at a moving contact point with a fixed contact angle. This is the model of a moving contact line at scales below the slip length, in its simplest setting. The slip length is the only length scale, and nothing is prescribed at the contact point beyond the angle: no relaxation law for the angle, and no contact-point dissipation. Slip removes the paradox found by Huh and Scriven, the infinite dissipation at a contact line that moves without slip, but in this model a weaker singularity remains. We give, to our knowledge, the first rigorous characterisation of this singularity for solutions of the free-boundary problem near the stationary state. For small contact angles and small initial data satisfying two compatibility conditions, we prove local existence, uniqueness and Lipschitz dependence on the data. The compatibility conditions are the price of the fixed angle for solutions regular in time up to the initial time. Rather than hiding the singularity, the solution class carries it explicitly in corner expansions. The velocity is continuous up to the contact point. The pressure has a logarithmic singularity, the slip-regularised version of that of Huh and Scriven. Its coefficient is proportional to the contact-point velocity. The slope of the free boundary has a corresponding logarithmic correction, the slip-scale counterpart of the Cox-Voinov relation. The linearised problem combines terms of different scaling, which prevents a direct treatment by the Mellin transform. We solve it by a Lax-Milgram argument, and an auxiliary test function problem shows that the variational solution satisfies the equations. Explicit Mellin representations then yield the corner expansions, and the nonlinear problem is solved by a contraction argument.

Let $X$ be a Riemann surface, $K_X \rightarrow X$ the canonical bundle, and $T_X\coloneqq K_X^{-1}\rightarrow X$ the dual bundle of the canonical bundle. For each integer $r \geq 2$, each $q \in H^0(K_X^r)$, and each choice of the square root $K_X^{1/2}$ of the canonical bundle, we canonically obtain a Higgs bundle $(\K_r,Φ(q))\rightarrow X$, which is called a cyclic Higgs bundle. A diagonal solution $h = (h_1, \dots, h_r)$ to the Hitchin equation on a cyclic Higgs bundle yields $r-1$ Hermitian metrics $H_1, \dots, H_{r-1}$ on $T_X\rightarrow X$, defined as $H_j \coloneqq h_j^{-1} \otimes h_{j+1}$ for each $j=1,\dots, r-1$, while $h_1$, $h_r$, and $q$ yield a Hermitian metric $H_r$ on $T_X \rightarrow X$ which is degenerate at the zero set of $q$. A diagonal solution is said to be complete if the Kähler metrics induced by $H_1,\dots, H_{r-1}$ are all complete. Li--Mochizuki established a theorem stating that, for any Riemann surface $X$ and any $q$ that is non-zero unless $X$ is hyperbolic, there exists a unique complete solution $h$ to the Hitchin equation for the cyclic Higgs bundle $(\K_r,Φ(q))$ with $\det(h)=1$. The holomorphic section $q$ induces a subharmonic weight function $φ_q=\frac{1}{r}\log|q|^2$ on $K_X\rightarrow X$, and the Hitchin equation depends on $q$ only through this weight function. In previous work, the author introduced a variant of the Hitchin equation associated with an arbitrary subharmonic weight function $\varphi$. In this paper, we extend the Li--Mochizuki theorem to complete solutions of the extended Hitchin equation associated to any subharmonic weight function $\varphi$ that is not identically $-\infty$ unless $X$ is hyperbolic.

We also obtain monotonicity and asymptotic behavior of the separation times and quantitative rates at which the corresponding normal derivatives vanish. For tangential data in \(n\geq3\), a separation time for the parallel component exists precisely when \(\partial_{x_1}R_1'ψ(x')>0\), with \(R_1'\) the first Riesz transform; log-concavity makes the separation time unique. We construct an autonomous Lipschitz fast dynamo on the flat three-torus whose particle flow has zero topological entropy and whose ideal induction equation has no exponential growth. We perform a multiscale construction starting from the Ponomarenko flow. For every sufficiently small positive magnetic diffusivity, the induction operator on $\mathbb{T}^3$ has an eigenvalue with real part bounded below by a positive constant independent of the diffusivity. A corresponding non-zero real-valued magnetic field satisfies an exact exponential growth law in $\mathrm{L}^2$. Moreover, the particle flow and its inverse have Lipschitz constants growing at most linearly in time and thus zero topological entropy. We consider controlled SDEs with measurable coefficients, a uniformly elliptic diffusion coefficient and an $L_d$-drift. In this framework we investigate the relationship among value functions, PDEs, and operator semigroups. First, for a cost with an infinite time horizon on a bounded domain, we identify the value function as an $L_{d_0}$-viscosity solution to an HJB equation and we establish quantitative regularity estimates. The constant $d_0 \in (d/2, d)$ only depends on the space dimension $d$, the ellipticity constants of the diffusion coefficient and the $L_d$-bound of the drift. To illustrate applications of these results, we provide a uniqueness theorem under an additional assumption on the diffusion coefficient, showing a stochastic representation, and we discuss stability of value functions. Second, we consider a cost with a finite time horizon, terminal and running terms, assuming an $L_{d + 1}$-drift. We show that the value function indexed over the terminal cost is a nonlinear semigroup on $C_b (\mathbb{R}^d)$ and we establish a regularization by noise effect, which shows that the semigroup regularizes lower semicontinuity to local Hölder continuity. We also establish quantitative regularity estimates for the semigroup that are local in time and global in space. Lastly, under an additional $L_{d + 2, loc}$-assumption on the drift, we relate the semigroup to a parabolic PDE, showing that the associated value function is an $L_{d + 1}$-viscosity solution. Our proofs of the regularity of the value functions, the $C_b$-Feller property of the semigroup and its regularization by noise effects are based on a strong Markov selection principle and analytic estimates for linear diffusions that were recently established by N. V. Krylov in a series of papers. We highlight that our method covers frameworks without uniqueness of the controlled SDEs, as well as the associated PDEs.

♻ ☆ The Capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Flows
Dongjing Ma, Peihe Wang, Hua Zhu
We study a capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski flow on a non-obtuse spherical cap for $1\le k\le n-1$: \[ \partial_t h= \frac{h^2\varphi(\ell/h)}{f}\, \barσ_k(\nabla^2h+hσ)-h, \qquad \nabla_μh=\cotθ\,h. \] In the supercritical regime \[ a_\varphi(s)=\frac{s\varphi'(s)}{\varphi(s)} \ge k+1+δ, \qquad s a_\varphi'(s)\ge0, \] we obtain time-uniform $C^0$ and $C^1$ estimates and a closed scalar equation for the speed ratio. A dynamic Orlicz square-completion identity, combined with inverse-concavity, yields a viscosity estimate for the minimum principal radius. Under a strict dynamic Orlicz-convexity condition and \[ \frac{f_μ}{f}\ge\frac{n-k}{n}\cotθ, \] we prove time-uniform two-sided principal-radius bounds on every smooth existence interval for $0<θ\leπ/2$ and deduce long-time existence and smooth convergence to a stationary solution. The boundary regularity step uses a quantitative interior concave estimate through Neumann reflection and a concave uniformly elliptic extension. Under the weaker condition $(f\ell^{k-1})_μ\ge0$, strict convexity is preserved on every smooth existence interval. For $k=1$, the transformed scalar equation is uniformly parabolic for every $0<θ<π$. Classical parabolic estimates then give an all-angle scalar flow theorem, without asserting geometric convexity preservation in the obtuse range.
♻ ☆ Existence of three solutions for parametric $p$-Laplacian equations in $\mathbb{R}^N$
E. Amoroso, G. D'Aguì
In this paper we deal with a nonlinear elliptic problem in the whole space $\mathbb{R}^N$ involving the $p$-Laplacian operator with $p>N$. Under suitable assumptions on the potential term and on the nonlinearity, we establish the existence of at least three distinct weak solutions. Our approach is variational and relies on two different three critical points theorems. The results extend to higher dimensions some recent multiplicity theorems for one-dimensional $p$-Laplacian equations on the real line, and provide explicit ranges for the parameter $λ> 0$ ensuring the existence of multiple solutions, which are nonnegative under additional sign conditions. The nontriviality of the solutions is also discussed. Finally, applications to problems whose nonlinearities have separated variables are presented.

♻ ☆ A Dynkin condition for manifolds with boundary
Marie Bormann, David Tewodrose
We propose a Dynkin-type condition for smooth Riemannian manifolds with boundary. We show that this condition implies bi-Lipschitz equivalence with a Bakry-Émery weighted Riemannian manifold obtained via a time change. As a consequence, we obtain various results, including a local doubling property as well as lower bounds on the Neumann spectral gap and logarithmic Sobolev constant. ♻ ☆ The Capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Problem
Hua Zhu
We study the Capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Problem on an acute spherical cap. For $1\le k\le n-1$, the equation is \[ h\,\varphi(\ell/h)\,\barσ_k(\nabla^2h+hσ)=f, \qquad \nabla_μh=\cotθ\,h, \] where $\ell$ is the support function of the unit capillary spherical cap. For $1\le k\le n-1$, this includes the capillary Christoffel--Minkowski and capillary $L_p$ Christoffel--Minkowski problems; the same density formally recovers the capillary Orlicz--Minkowski endpoint when $k=n$. We organize the theory in five parts. After recalling the elementary symmetric functions and the capillary support-function formalism, we review the capillary Orlicz--Brunn--Minkowski framework and introduce the intermediate-order Orlicz $k$-mixed functional and its Euler--Lagrange equation. In the supercritical regime \[ a_\varphi(t):=\frac{t\varphi'(t)}{\varphi(t)}\ge k+1+δ, \] we derive uniform $C^0$, $C^1$ and $C^2$ estimates for positive $k$-admissible solutions. The same supercritical index produces a strictly coercive second variation and a spectral gap for the linearized Neumann operator. These facts lead to existence and uniqueness by a continuity method, quantitative stability of the solution map in both the datum and the Orlicz weight, and an open perturbative class of strictly convex non-power solutions. Under an additional capillary Orlicz-convexity condition on the datum, a full-rank argument upgrades the global admissible solution to a strictly convex capillary support function.
♻ ☆ The retarded interaction and non-scattering for 3D Maxwell--Dirac system
Yonggeun Cho, Kiyeon Lee
We prove an a priori obstruction to linear scattering for the massive Maxwell--Dirac system in three space dimensions. A global solution with nonzero charge cannot scatter linearly in $L^2$ if its full and homogeneous potentials are $O(t^{-1})$, and the homogeneous potential is $o(t^{-1})$ in compact timelike cones. No nonlinear asymptotic expansion is assumed in this non-scattering theorem. We also identify the exact leading interaction when the nonlinear current approaches a free Dirac current in $L^1$. Its coefficient is a positive quadratic form in the velocity density and is bounded below by the square of the charge divided by $4π$. The proof uses free Dirac asymptotics and an estimate for retarded source errors after pairing with a smooth free current.

♻ ☆ Uniqueness of synchronized stationary equilibria in the Kuramoto mean field game
Sebastian Munoz
The Kuramoto mean field game describes a population of oscillators which, above a critical value of the interaction parameter, form synchronized Nash equilibria. We show that these synchronized equilibria are unique, up to rotations, for each value of the parameter. Moreover, the unique equilibrium depends smoothly on the interaction parameter, and converges smoothly to the uniform distribution when the parameter approaches its critical value. These statements are direct consequences of our main technical result: the self-consistency map is strictly concave, as was previously conjectured by Carmona, Cormier, and Soner. In the proof, we decompose the second derivative of the self-consistency map as the sum of two moments, and prove that each of them is negative by using symmetrization arguments to exploit hidden monotonicity and skewness properties of the equilibria.

♻ ☆ Non-Ljusternik--Schnirelman eigenvalues of the pure $p$-Laplacian exist
Vladimir Bobkov
An old and well-known open problem in the critical point theory asks whether, for some $p \neq 2$ and some bounded domain $Ω$, there exists a critical value of the $p$-Dirichlet energy $\|\nabla u\|_{p;Ω}^p$ over an $L^p(Ω)$-sphere in $W_0^{1,p}(Ω)$ lying outside of a Ljusternik--Schnirelman type sequence of critical values, the latter will be called LS eigenvalues of the $p$-Laplacian. In this work, we provide a positive answer by showing the existence of a non-LS eigenvalue when $p>2$ is sufficiently close to $2$ and $Ω$ is just a planar rectangle close to the square. The arguments pursue the observation that a simple eigenvalue of the Laplacian can be a common point for several branches of eigenvalues of the $p$-Laplacian as $p$ varies. Since LS eigenvalues are continuous with respect to $p$ and exhaust the whole spectrum when $p=2$, we deduce that at least one of the branches must contain non-LS eigenvalues.

♻ ☆ Flexibility of the isometric immersion system in arbitrary dimension and codimension and the energy scaling of prestrained thin films
Marta Lewicka, Hui Li
We prove that, for a given $C^{r,β}$-regular Riemann metric posed on a $d$-dimensional domain, every short immersion into the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^{d+k}$, can be uniformly approximated by exact isometric immersions of regularity $C^{1,α}$ for any $α<α_0=\min\{\frac{r+β}{2}, \frac{1}{1+d(d+1)/k}\}$. Our theorem recovers several previously known results as special cases. The novelty thereof lies in providing a unified flexibility statement for arbitrary dimensions $d$ and codimensions $k$, while also treating the so far uncharted range $k\in (1, \frac{d(d+1)}{2}-d+1)\setminus \{d\}$, where no corresponding general result was previously available. Our threshold flexibility exponent $α_0$ agrees with that previously obtained for the closely related Monge-Ampère system. As an application, we prove a new estimate in the quantitative immersability of thin prestrained films, setting the scaling exponent of the infimum of non-Euclidean energies in presence of an arbitrary prestrain metric, and in the limit of the film's vanishing thickness, at $\frac{4α_0}{α_0+1}$.

♻ ☆ A variational Free Boundary Ricci flow on Surfaces with Boundary
Jean C. Cortissoz, Juan J. Villamarín
We study a Ricci flow on a compact surface with boundary arising as the L2-gradient flow of the Liouville functional with its natural Neumann boundary condition. Geometrically, this boundary condition preserves the geodesic-curvature density H dσ. In the regime in which the total scalar curvature satisfies 0 < C_0 < 4π, a scale invariant normalised Liouville functional is monotone, and bounded below. In our first result, we use its dissipation to show that every compact blow-up limit is homothetically shrinking with constant positive scalar curvature. We then treat a rotationally symmetric disc with H_0 > 0 and C_0 > 0, in which case every noncompact limit is ruled out via singularity analysis and a noncollapsing theorem. Consequently, the normalised flow fully converges smoothly to the unique spherical cap determined by the initial area and the preserved boundary data, yielding our second result. Additionally, we also study the regime in which C0 is nonpositive. In this case standard PDE arguments prove full smooth convergence of the normalised flow towards a metric with constant nonpositive scalar curvature.
♻ ☆ The Lee-Huang-Yang Formula in the Hard-Core Simplified Approach to the Bose gas
Mohamed El Hedi Bahri, Ian Jauslin
We study the hard-core variant of the Simplified Approach to the ground state of the dilute Bose gas. The hard-core potential has been the subject of renewed attention, and is physically relevant to realistic atomic Bose gases. The hard-core Simple Equation is an integro-differential equation, and we construct its solution via a monotone iteration scheme and prove existence and uniqueness (in a restricted sense) of the solution. The energy per particle $e$ and the density $ρ$ of the solution are shown to satisfy the Lee-Huang-Yang formula $e = 2πρ(1 + \frac{128}{15\sqrtπ}\sqrtρ + o(\sqrtρ))$ as $ρ\to 0$, and the condensate fraction $η$ predicted by the hard-core Simple Equation is shown to satisfy $η= 1 - \frac{8}{3\sqrtπ}\sqrtρ + o(\sqrtρ)$ as $ρ\to 0$, in agreement with Bogolyubov's theory. We thus extend results of Carlen, Jauslin, Lieb to the hard-core case. The hard-core equation is defined on its own terms, and the proofs proceed by approximating the hard-core potential with the soft-core potentials $m\,χ_{\{|x| \le 1\}}$ of increasing height $m$: at fixed energy, we establish the $L^1$ convergence of the corresponding solutions and the convergence of their densities at an $O(m^{-1/2})$ rate, and we show that the Lee-Huang-Yang expansions of the energy and of the condensate fraction for the soft-core equations hold with errors uniform in $m$, so that they survive the hard-core limit.
♻ ☆ Asymptotic analysis of Dirichlet problems in supercritically perforated domains via quantification by torsional rigidity
Naoto Sato
We study the Dirichlet problem $-\mathrm{div}(A^{\varepsilon}\nabla u^{\varepsilon}) = f$ on varying open sets $D^{\varepsilon}$, with uniformly elliptic coefficients $A^{\varepsilon}$, in the regime where the solutions vanish in the limit for every source. For periodically perforated domains, this is the supercritical regime. We show that the torsional rigidity $T(D^{\varepsilon})$ is the natural normalization: up to a subsequence, $u^{\varepsilon}/T(D^{\varepsilon})$ converges weakly as measures to $kf$ for every continuous source $f$, where $k$ is a nonzero finite measure independent of $f$, which we call the effective measure. The key ingredient is an estimate comparing $u^{\varepsilon}$ with the product of $f$ and the torsion function, whose rate depends on the domains only through $T(D^{\varepsilon})$. We also show that this rate is optimal. No structural assumption on the perforation is needed, and the results hold for relaxed Dirichlet problems. Every nonzero finite measure arises as an effective measure, so the continuity of the source cannot be dropped in general. For rougher sources, we characterize the convergence by a condition on the domains alone, expressed through their torsion functions or, equivalently, their Poincaré constants. We also prove that the effective measure is local, satisfies optimal two-sided bounds and is monotone with respect to the coefficients, and we study the role of the antisymmetric parts of the coefficients.

♻ ☆ A nonlocal transmission problem on a hybrid continuous-discrete domain
Hafida Abbas, Abdelhalim Azzouz
We study a quadratic nonlocal variational problem on a hybrid domain formed by a compact interval and finitely many discrete points. The associated energy splits into continuous, discrete, and interface contributions. Our main estimate shows that the interface term yields a coercive coupling between the two phases and provides an equivalent hybrid norm. As a consequence, we prove existence and uniqueness of a minimizer for the corresponding variational problem and characterize it as the unique weak solution of the associated hybrid Euler--Lagrange system. The latter combines a nonlocal integral equation on the continuous component with a finite nonlocal algebraic system on the discrete nodes.

We first prove local well-posedness, together with a global existence criterion and a blow-up criterion for the maximal solution. Our main result is that every global solution $u\in C\big([0,+\infty),\dot{H}^{1/2}_{a,1}(\mathbb{R}^3)\big)$ satisfies $\|u(t)\|_{\dot{H}^{1/2}_{a,1}}\to0$ as $t\to+\infty$. The proof combines the classical decay of global solutions in $\dot{H}^{1/2}$ with an analyticity estimate for small data in $\dot{H}^{1/2}$ and Fourier-analytic product laws in Sobolev--Gevrey spaces. As consequences, we obtain the decay rate $\|u(t)\|_{\dot{H}^s}=o\big(t^{-\frac{s-1/2}{2}}\big)$ for every $s\ge\frac12$, and the stability of global solutions under small perturbations of the initial data in $\dot{H}^{1/2}_{a,1}$.

☆ Fourier Algebras of HLS Groupoids: Lifts, Amenability, and Spectrum
Joseph DeGaetani, Mahya Ghandehari
We investigate the Fourier algebra of a certain class of groupoids, called the HLS groupoids, within Paterson's continuous framework for locally compact groupoids. We develop the basic harmonic analysis of HLS groupoids by obtaining concrete descriptions of their topology, representations, and Fourier algebra. We then study the restriction maps from the Fourier algebra $A(\mathcal{G})$ of an HLS groupoid $\mathcal{G}$ to the Fourier algebras of its isotropy subgroups, and construct explicit norm-preserving lifts for these restriction maps. As applications, we describe the norm of every element of $A(\mathcal{G})$ in terms of the norms of its restrictions to the isotropy subgroups. We prove an analogue of Leptin's theorem characterizing when $A(\mathcal{G})$ has a bounded approximate identity. We also show that the Gelfand spectrum of $A(\mathcal{G})$ is homeomorphic to $\mathcal{G}$. Finally, using abstract arguments that, unlike our methods for HLS groupoids, do not yield explicit constructions, we show that norm-preserving lifts exist and that the Gelfand spectrum of the Fourier algebra is homeomorphic to the groupoid for every étale groupoid. This generalizes Eymard's theorem and answers a question of Paterson for étale groupoids.
☆ A Counterexample to Voiculescu's Normal Dilation Conjecture
Xiang Tang

This gives counterexamples to Voiculescu's normal dilation and stable classification conjectures. The construction uses magnetic shifts on finite square tori. Their real parts have commutators of uniformly bounded trace norm, while their frame errors admit logarithmic lower bounds in the lattice size. A summability criterion for frame error turns these finite-dimensional estimates into a compact counterexample. The same operator inequalities yield a rank profile invariant under Hilbert-Schmidt perturbations and normal stabilization, which distinguishes the example from zero.

Let G be an infinite compact abelian group and let K={0,a_1,a_2,...}, where a_1>a_2>...>0 and a_n\to 0. We construct a nonzero real, even, purely singular Rajchman measure whose Fourier--Stieltjes range is contained in K. We then classify the compact abelian groups on which every positive null palette is exactly realizable in each of four classes: purely singular measures, atomless purely singular measures, strongly continuous purely singular measures, and Rajchman purely singular measures. Exact realization by a purely singular measure is always possible; atomless exact realization fails precisely for groups topologically isomorphic to \mathbb{T}\times F with F finite; and universal exact Rajchman realization is equivalent to \operatorname{Tor}(\widehat G) being infinite, or equivalently to G/G_0 being infinite. Finally, if U\subset\mathbb{C} is open and 0\in\overline U, we construct a continuous Rajchman measure with nonzero singular part whose Fourier--Stieltjes range is contained in U, assuming metrizability of G when 0\notin U. ☆ A description of the space with no separable quotient presented by OpenAI

OpenAI recently presented a remarkable solution to the longstanding separable quotient problem in Banach space theory. The result establishes its independence from ZFC, relative to the consistency of ZFC with a measurable cardinal. Under the continuum hypothesis, the paper constructs a nonseparable Banach space $X$ with no separable infinite-dimensional quotient. The present paper offers an alternative exposition of the mechanism leading to $X$ and its properties. Our aim is to make the methods and results more accessible and to offer a clearer understanding of this exotic space.

☆ Boundedness properties of bilinear Fourier integral operators with complex phases

In this paper, we investigate mapping properties on Lebesgue spaces of bilinear Fourier integral operators (FIOs) with complex phases. Indeed, we provide for bilinear Fourier integral operators with complex phases boundedness theorems for the corresponding Seeger-Sogge-Stein orders, including the endpoint estimates. Our results extend the same boundedness property in the case of real-valued phases proved by Rodriguez-López, Rule, and Staubach, and provide the bilinear version for the linear one proved earlier by Ruzhansky for phases of positive type. For this, a maximal function theorem due to Bourgain is applied. As a byproduct, we also consider transference boundedness theorems of FIOs with complex phases from $\mathbb{R}^n$ to the torus $\mathbb{T}^n\equiv \mathbb{R}^n/\mathbb{Z}^n$ and then, we provide new criteria for the boundedness of Fourier integral operators on the torus with complex phases (Fourier series operators in the sense of Ruzhansky and Turunen).

We study the problem of choosing $m$ landmark points so that the span of the kernel translates is as close as possible to the leading $s$-dimensional eigenspace of a positive-definite kernel. The natural measure is the Hilbert-Schmidt operator discrepancy between the reproducing-kernel-Hilbert-space (RKHS) projectors onto the two subspaces. We give a closed form spectral alignment function in terms of the truncated Mercer kernel and relate it to the classical integrated power function (Nyström trace error) through a two-sided sandwich bound. Minimizing the function by gradient descent on the landmark coordinates produces landmark sets that are evenly spaced. Theoretical results show that optimal configurations are those whose eigenfunction sampling matrix is a scaled isometry. On homogeneous spaces these are exactly the minimal equal-weight cubature rules for products of leading eigenfunctions, and for every $m\ge s$ they are the configurations whose sampled eigenfunctions form a unit-norm tight frame. Experiments on $\mathbb{S}^1$ and $\mathbb{S}^2$ agree with the theory. On the circle, with $s\le2m$ and a moderate bandwidth, every random start converges to equispaced landmarks, and on the sphere the optimizer recovers the regular tetrahedron, octahedron, and icosahedron from random starts. Finally, we analyze the numerical conditioning of the problem.

Marek Lassak, Stanislaw J. Szarek
The Banach-Mazur distance is one of the standard tools used in the study of mathematical objects such as convex bodies or normed spaces, and it becomes indispensable when investigating properties that are invariant under linear isomorphisms. It appears in convex geometry and convex analysis as a way to quantify the approximation of convex bodies. In functional analysis, it plays a basic role in the study of local properties of Banach spaces. The goal of this survey is to present a cohesive picture of these two perspectives. We supply an extensive collection of known results for reference and list open problems of varying difficulty, which could stimulate further research. We include in our discussion several distinct variations on the concept of the Banach-Mazur distance, some of them exploratory, that haven't received much attention to date in the literature. We follow the trend - which emerged in recent decades - of considering arbitrary convex bodies, and not just those that are centrally symmetric. Finally, we include a comprehensive list of references on the Banach-Mazur distance.

As a corollary, we show that various stochastic control problems, e.g. optimal stopping and mean-variance portfolio selection, are stable under bounded, measurable drift perturbations. Additionally, we derive concentration inequalities (with respect to certain dynamic risk measures) for stochastic integrals $\int H_s dX_s$ and deduce appropriate bounds on their tail behavior. Furthermore, using the functional Itô formula, we show that the AQTCI for $\text{Law}(X)$ allows one to deduce classical transport inequalities for $\text{Law}(F(X))$ even when $F$ is not Lipschitz on path space. For every measurable fundamental domain $K$ and nonzero vector $ξ$ in the dual lattice $Λ^*$, we observe the sharp directional variance estimate \[ \left\langle \operatorname{Cov}_K ξ,ξ\right\rangle \geq \frac{1}{12}. \] This yields a lower bound on the torus spectral gap $λ_{\mathrm{SG}}(\mathbb{T}_Λ)$ (equivalently, the length of the shortest nonzero dual vector $λ_1(Λ^*)$) in terms of the maximal covariance of $K$: \[ λ_{\mathrm{SG}}(\mathbb{T}_Λ) = 4π^2 λ_1(Λ^*)^2 \geq \frac{π^2}{3\left\|\operatorname{Cov}_K\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}}. \] Analogous sharp results are obtained for the isoperimetric profile and the Cheeger constant $D_{\mathrm{Che}}(\mathbb{T}_Λ)$ using an old argument of Hadwiger. In particular, when the Voronoi cell $K_Λ$ of a lattice with $\det Λ= 1$ is isotropic, the recent resolution of the Slicing Problem by Klartag and Lehec implies that \[ D_{\mathrm{Che}}(\mathbb{T}_Λ),\quad λ_{\mathrm{SG}}(\mathbb{T}_Λ),\quad λ_1(Λ^*) \geq c > 0, \] where $c > 0$ is a universal constant independent of dimension $n$; this may be thought of as a positive resolution of the Kannan--Lovász--Simonovits conjecture for all flat tori. While there are lattices $Λ$ and corresponding Voronoi cells $K = K_Λ$ for which no dimension-independent converse inequality to the spectral-gap bound above can hold, we show that under a certain sectional tiling hypothesis, this inequality is in fact an equivalence (up to numerical constants).

An old and well-known open problem in the critical point theory asks whether, for some $p \neq 2$ and some bounded domain $Ω$, there exists a critical value of the $p$-Dirichlet energy $\|\nabla u\|_{p;Ω}^p$ over an $L^p(Ω)$-sphere in $W_0^{1,p}(Ω)$ lying outside of a Ljusternik--Schnirelman type sequence of critical values, the latter will be called LS eigenvalues of the $p$-Laplacian. In this work, we provide a positive answer by showing the existence of a non-LS eigenvalue when $p>2$ is sufficiently close to $2$ and $Ω$ is just a planar rectangle close to the square. The arguments pursue the observation that a simple eigenvalue of the Laplacian can be a common point for several branches of eigenvalues of the $p$-Laplacian as $p$ varies. Moreover, for normal channels with $σ$-finite codomain, we prove that the BS channel divergence of Hollands and Ranallo coincides with the extended norm of our operator-valued divergence. Finally, we give finite-dimensional examples and obtain an explicit formula for a finite-index conditional expectation. In the BS case, this formula reduces to the logarithm of the Jones--Kosaki index.
♻ ☆ Zong's problem on $2d$ half-spaces containing the unit ball

We prove that the intersection of $2d$ half-spaces containing the Euclidean unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^d$ contains a point of norm at least $\sqrt{d}$. Equality in the radius bound characterizes the cube up to orthogonal transformations. The proof gives a lower bound for the average squared norm of the vertices, weighted by the Gaussian measures of their normal cones. This estimate follows from an inequality for the Gaussian measures of a simplicial cone and its projected facets, which in turn reduces to a linear estimate for the Gaussian centroid of a simplicial cone. We also discuss a quadratic extension of the problem and give a bound for it using an independent spectral argument. This bound implies that the intersection of any $m > d$ half-spaces containing the unit ball contains a point of norm at least $\sqrt{m}\,\ln\frac{m}{m-d}$.

☆ Soft-constrained Schrödinger bridge for generative AI: numerical algorithms and approximation guarantees
Jin Ma, Ying Tan, Renyuan Xu, Qinxin Yan
We study a soft-constrained formulation of the Schrödinger bridge problem, in which the terminal distribution constraint is relaxed into a penalty on the discrepancy between the terminal law of the controlled process and a target distribution. This leads to an unconstrained McKean--Vlasov stochastic control problem, where the interaction enters only through the terminal cost. We characterize the optimizer via a McKean--Vlasov forward-backward stochastic differential equation and establish well-posedness under very mild assumptions. We also analyze two approximation regimes relevant to data-driven computation: approximation of the target law by empirical samples, and finite-particle approximation of the McKean--Vlasov control problem. For both, we derive convergence results and error estimates. Finally, building on the well-posedness and approximation results, we investigate two neural numerical methods: one based on the forward-backward system and the other on direct control optimization. Both methods are tested on state-of-the-art generative tasks. Our results provide both an algorithmic foundation and its theoretical guarentee for soft-constrained Schrödinger bridge problems in sample-based generative modeling.

As our main contribution, we establish three new equivalent characterizations of these spaces. Second, we give a thorough functional analytic treatment of the nonlocal $ρ$-Laplacian $Δ^ρ$, which allows us to represent general nonlocal Sobolev spaces through its square root $(-Δ^ρ)^{1/2}$. Third, we show that $H^{ρ,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ coincides with the image $g_ρ* L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ for a suitable convolution kernel $g_ρ\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^n)$, which confirms that these spaces are genuine potential spaces. In this spirit, the present work can also be viewed as introducing a natural notion of generalized Bessel potential spaces.

We derive the Boltzmann equation from the Newtonian dynamics of particles interacting through a short-range repulsive potential for arbitrarily long times, in the Boltzmann--Grad limit. This extends the recent hard-sphere result of Deng, Hani and Ma (arXiv:2408.07818) to short-range potentials. Compared with hard spheres, two new difficulties arise: (i) in the absence of a Burago--Ferleger--Kononenko-type bound (Ann. of Math. 147 (1998), 695--708, doi:10.2307/120962), a bounded number of particles may undergo an unbounded number of collisions within a short time; and (ii) since collisions last a positive time, three or more particles may interact simultaneously. To overcome (i), we treat such clusters of recollisions as single objects, called boxes, keeping track only of their entry and exit structure, so that internal collisions do not enter the combinatorial counting. The multi-particle collisions in (ii), together with the boxes, lead to more complicated molecules, which requires adapting the counting estimates and the cutting algorithm.

As a result, we obtain densely many counterexamples to the Bethe-Sommerfeld Conjecture (BSC) for divergence-form operators. Moreover, we prove that the thin-layer construction controls the gap topology: by carefully selecting the seed medium, one can realize a single operator with any prescribed configuration of gap Chern numbers. This is the first of two papers that contains all the fundamental ingredients for the thin-layer induction. In the second paper, we will apply this framework to disprove the BSC for the full three-dimensional Maxwell operator.

Rational root isolation certifies the two-step global minimizers. With diffusion in one space dimension, nonnegative bounded $H^1$ initial data and positive diffusivities, the costs, weighted gradients and Hessians differ by $O(τ)$ uniformly in the spatial mesh, where $τ$ is the time step. A uniform positive lower bound on the reduced Hessian gives the same order for the distance between nearby controls. A large enough effort penalty gives unique global discrete minimizers. We also prove positivity, exact population balance and a common variational limit, and derive exact discrete adjoints and Hessian actions. Numerical tests trace changes in curvature and stationary controls across parameters and grids, with costs evaluated on a common reference using adaptive time stepping. The construction extends to weighted production--destruction systems, giving exact harvest accounting and smooth derivatives on fixed grids.

For one-dimensional transport systems satisfying the Kalman rank condition, this yields localized observability in the intrinsic Kalman--Jordan energy space for arbitrary real Jordan structure and nonzero speeds. For unions of observed intervals with a uniform positive lower length bound, the sharp condition is that the slowest characteristic travels farther than the gap supremum. Observability fails at equality even when this supremum is not attained. Duality gives exact controllability in the dual energy space. We also obtain sharp criteria for translating observation regions and scalar transport with an integrable convolution kernel. The reconstruction hypothesis is also necessary for observability. An anisotropic heat-flux example shows that it applies beyond coercive multiplication-plus-compact Gramian decompositions.

The occurrence of plasma echoes, or even a growing cascade in a reduced model, does not by itself establish this stability. We prove that the amplification persists under changes in the linearized operator, including collisions and the exact evolving background coefficients, and under nonlinear perturbations. This yields optimality of the exponent $1/3$ obtained by Chaturvedi, Luk, and Nguyen in the Sobolev stability threshold. Specifically, we construct solutions with initial Sobolev perturbations of size $ν^{1/3}[\log(1/ν)]^p$ whose transport profiles exhibit norm inflation before the enhanced-dissipation time scale $ν^{-1/3}$. Since collisions preclude the backward Sobolev construction used in collisionless echo arguments, we prepare the initial data at physical time zero and control the entire forward evolution.

☆ Controllability of Acoustic Waves by Point Sources: Reachable States and Stable Reconstruction
Kais Ammari, Mourad Sini
We study the terminal controllability of the three-dimensional acoustic wave equation driven by finitely many fixed point sources, with zero initial data and time-dependent amplitudes supported in a finite interval. Although finitely many fixed sources cannot control the whole energy space, we establish the following results: (i) For source amplitudes in the first-order Sobolev space in time, the terminal state has finite energy if and only if all amplitudes vanish at both endpoints of the control interval. (ii) We derive an exact frequency-domain identity for the terminal energy involving a Gram matrix whose diagonal entries are one and whose off-diagonal entries are given by the sinc function, depending on frequency and source separation. (iii) For every positive control time, the terminal control operator is bounded below and is an isomorphism onto its closed reachable range, which has infinite codimension even among states satisfying the finite-propagation support condition. (iv) We establish a necessary and sufficient radiation-field criterion for reachability, provide stable reconstruction of the unique controls, and characterize the best approximation of non-reachable targets. The optimal coercivity constant equals one before the shortest source travel time. At long times, it decays as the inverse square of the control time for two sources and as the inverse fourth power for three equally spaced collinear sources. We also obtain upper bounds for general configurations and illustrate the theoretical results through reproducible Galerkin computations.

This paper concerns entire minimizing four-junction solutions to a two-dimensional Allen-Cahn system with a four-well potential. In a suitable regime of unequal surface tensions, the construction yields a family of solutions with varying opening angles of phase sectors. The proof employs two-direction slicing arguments for tight energy bounds and localization of the diffuse interface, together with a new iteration scheme that controls change of approximating sharp interfaces at successively smaller scales.

We study the Dirichlet problem for the octonionic Monge-Ampere equation on smooth bounded domains in the octonionic plane $\mathbb{O}^2\cong\mathbb{R}^{16}$. For a smooth positive density that is nondecreasing in the unknown function, we prove existence and uniqueness of a smooth strictly plurisubharmonic solution whenever there is a smooth strictly plurisubharmonic subsolution with the prescribed boundary values. The result also holds on relatively compact domains with smooth boundary in flat translation quotients. On smooth bounded strictly octonionic pseudoconvex domains, we construct the unique Green function with zero boundary values and singularity $-|q-a|^{-6}+O(1)$ at an interior pole $a$. We prove $C^{1,1}$ regularity locally up to the boundary away from the pole, together with sharp bounds for the gradient and the full real Hessian. The proof combines boundary estimates based on translations and spin rotations with weighted estimates obtained by differentiating along rotations and dilations.
☆ The topological degree of the regular $SU(3)$ Toda system

We resolve the long-standing open problem of computing the Leray--Schauder degree of the regular $SU(3)$ Toda system on a closed oriented surface $M$. If $d_{m,k}$ denotes the degree in the block $(4πm,4π(m+1))\times(4πk,4π(k+1))$, then \[ \sum_{m,k\geq0}d_{m,k}x^my^k =(1-x)^{χ(M)-1}(1-y)^{χ(M)-1}(1-xy)^{χ(M)}, \] where $χ(M)$ is the Euler characteristic of $M$. Nonvanishing of $d_{m,k}$ thus gives an existence criterion in terms of the topology of $M$ and the parameter block. At each step of the degree computation, we show that the only possible local mass pairs are $(4π,0)$ and $(8π,4π)$. We use generic perturbations and local second-order information on the weights to exclude collisions of shadow centers and splitting at mixed blow-up points. The shadow degrees and the Morse index then give the degree jump at each critical value.

For $α>1$, we obtain a second solution for $h=u^{4α-1}e^{u^{4α}}$, provided that the maximum of the first solution exceeds a constant depending only on $α$. For $α\leq1$, this question remains open.

We study subwavelength resonances of a finite chain of $N\ge2$ close-to-touching spherical resonators in three dimensions with a single radius defect of relative size $τ\in(0,1]$ and gap width $\varepsilon$. Taking the high-contrast limit before the narrow-gap limit, we prove that the positive generalized eigenvalues of the weighted chain coupling matrix with respect to the volume matrix determine the leading relative resonant frequencies. After eliminating the finite tails, we obtain an exact characteristic determinant and identify a unique critical ratio $τ_*\in(0,1)$ at which the largest eigenvalue crosses the upper edge of the homogeneous recurrence band $[0,4]$. For every $0<τ<τ_*$, exactly one eigenvalue lies above this band, and its eigenvector decays geometrically along the tails. As $τ\toτ_*^-$, its recurrence decay length diverges like $(τ_*-τ)^{-1/2}$. As $τ\to0$, exactly one eigenvalue diverges like $τ^{-2}$ and its eigenvector concentrates at the defect; if the defect is interior, one additional positive eigenvalue has order $τ$. For suitably normalized relative resonant modes, the sequential limit of the $\varepsilon$-scaled gradient supremum in each gap equals the absolute difference between adjacent reduced amplitudes. For the largest-eigenvalue mode, this yields defect-adjacent gradient concentration as the defect shrinks.

☆ Geomagnetic Q-Response Inversion as a Calderón-Type Inverse Boundary Value Problem
Xinpeng Huang, Zhengyong Ren, Jingtian Tang
Whether electrical conductivity can be uniquely determined from magnetic measurements alone is a fundamental question in geomagnetic induction sounding. For a spherical conductor in the magnetoquasistatic model, we establish an equivalence between the complete Q-response and a restricted magnetic boundary operator, connecting geomagnetic induction to Calderon-type inverse boundary value theory. For axisymmetric conductivities, we derive exact representations of the zero-frequency zonal response derivatives as conductivity-weighted spatial moments. These formulas give an explicit interpretation of individual response derivatives, and completeness of the moment family yields conductivity uniqueness. For layered axisymmetric models with known shell interfaces and piecewise-constant radial dependence, we further establish uniqueness at a single nonzero frequency. Finite-dimensional subclasses also admit uniqueness and stability estimates from finitely many response coefficients at sufficiently low nonzero frequencies. These results identify complementary mechanisms for conductivity recovery from magnetic-only observations, while uniqueness for general three-dimensional scalar conductivities from ideal magnetic-only Q-response data remains unresolved.
☆ Uniqueness of invariant measures for mean-field stochastic damped wave and heat equations

We study invariant measures for a Wick-renormalized mean-field stochastic damped wave equation on the two-dimensional torus and for the corresponding stochastic heat equation. With Wick ordering relative to the massive Gaussian free field with covariance $(1-Δ)^{-1}$, we prove uniqueness among invariant laws whose renormalized second moment belongs to $H^{-σ}(\mathbb T^2)$, where $0<σ<\tfrac12$. Stationarity reduces the mean-field equation to a linear equation with a deterministic distribution-valued potential. We show that self-consistency forces this deterministic potential to vanish. The damped wave equation therefore has invariant law $\mathcal N(0,(1-Δ)^{-1})\otimes\mathcal N(0,\varepsilon^{-2}I)$, with covariance understood distributionally, while the heat equation has the Gaussian free field as its invariant law. This resolves self-consistency for spatially varying distribution-valued potentials and establishes uniqueness in the specified class. As the inertia parameter tends to zero, the position marginal remains equal to the invariant law of the corresponding stochastic heat equation, whereas the velocity marginal assigns vanishing probability to every bounded subset of $H^{-1-σ}(\mathbb T^2)$, establishing Smoluchowski-Kramers type behavior.

This paper is concerned with the time-periodic solutions of the Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann (VPB) system with a given time-periodic external force in the whole space $\mathbb{R}^3$, where the force is allowed to be non-potential. For the purpose, we first study the Cauchy problem around global Maxwellians, proving the global existence of small-amplitude solutions in a hybrid function space that combines the low-frequency Besov framework for the forced Boltzmann equation with a corresponding control of the self-consistent electric field. One key point occurs to the nonlinear Vlasov force $-\nabla_{x}φ\cdot \nabla_{v}f + \frac{1}{2}v \cdot \nabla_{x}φf$ at low frequencies. Rather than treating it as a generic source term, we exploit the Poisson equation and macroscopic balance laws to recover the structural cancellation required for the VPB semi-group estimates, which combined with high-frequency energy estimates and weighted microscopic propagation, yields a closed global well-posedness theory. We further prove uniform stability of the difference of two small-amplitude solutions driven by the same force with respect to distinct initial data. As a consequence of those results, for the time-periodic problem where the external force is time-periodic, we are able to make use of Serrin's method to establish the existence of a unique time-periodic solution of the same period together with its large time asymptotic stability. Our result also gives the existence and stability of stationary solutions when the external force is time-independent.

We study higher-order isometric liftings of bounded operators on Hilbert spaces under convexity and concavity assumptions. First, we prove that every $m$-convex operator $T$ satisfying $\sup_{n\geq 1}n^{-(m-1)}\|T^n\|^2<\infty$ admits a minimal $m$-isometric lifting whose complementary diagonal entry is an expansive $(m-1)$-isometric weighted shift. Next, we show that every $m$-concave operator admits a minimal $m$-isometric lifting with an expansive $m$-isometric weighted-shift component, without imposing an additional growth assumption. We also establish an alternation between convexity and concavity under polynomial growth conditions and give examples illustrating limitations of converse implications.

Ilya A. Krishtal, Jian Wu
How few observations are needed for the stable recovery of the initial state of a linear dynamical system? We study this question for systems governed by a positive operator, with fixed sensors and freely chosen sampling times and positive weights. Our main tool is an interpolation theorem for translates of a nonzero continuous integrable totally positive function. For every uniformly separated sequence of centers, we choose one node near each center so that the corresponding collocation operator is boundedly invertible. The displacement, node separation, and operator bounds depend only on the kernel and the lower separation of the centers; no upper bound is needed on their gaps. If a single integer orbit is a frame, we construct weighted Riesz bases whose sampling counts attain the spectral lower bound up to a bounded additive error. The same method yields bases from continuous functional calculus, including explicit resolvent bases. In the case of normal operators, we give a single-orbit frame for which every admissible weighted design has sampling count growing faster than the radial spectral count.

We show that every surjective isometry between two such projective cones is induced by a lattice isomorphism, possibly composed with the inversion map, and that the inversion occurs precisely when the vector lattice is a bounded inverse closed $f$-algebra. In particular, two such projective cones are isometric if and only if the underlying vector lattices are lattice isomorphic, and we determine the corresponding isometry groups. We apply these results to spaces of Hölder continuous functions, absolutely continuous functions, and continuous functions of bounded variation, for which we describe the surjective isometries explicitly. Finally, we show that the projective cones of these spaces of functions on an interval all have the same metric completion, but that no two of them are isometric.

Our main result characterizes this completion as the Bochner space, under an admissibility condition on jointly measurable stochastic Taylor coefficients. The proof uses dyadic piecewise linear interpolation to approximate integrable continuous stochastic processes in the expected uniform norm. Thus, the completed SMTMF space encompasses the full class of integrable continuous random functions on a compact time interval.

The extension is a left gyrotranslation composed with an isometry preserving the identity, gyroaddition, and scalar multiplication. Gyromidpoints and point reflections give continuation of local isometry germs. Without assuming simple connectedness, a global bijective isometric extension exists exactly when the germs of the map and its inverse are fixed by their respective monodromy actions. Continuity of each fixed-scalar multiplication map implies contractibility and hence simple connectedness. We construct standard-norm GGVs for $t>0$ on positive invertible cones of nonzero unital JB-algebras and, in dimension greater than one, on their projective cones. Power maps relate their gyrometrics to Thompson's and Hilbert's metrics, respectively, with equality at $t=1$. Thus for both metrics, bijective isometries between nonempty connected open subsets extend uniquely to global bijective isometries. We give proofs of the known Thompson and Hilbert isometry classifications, together with their power-coordinate forms for every $t>0$, using the GGV Mazur--Ulam theorem and recovering the Jordan structures from infinitesimal gyrations. Applications include a new proof of Mankiewicz's theorem on connected open subsets of real normed spaces and a local extension theorem for hyperbolic balls in real inner product spaces, including incomplete and infinite-dimensional spaces. We also give constructions for products and function spaces.

Let $K$ be a nonempty compact semialgebraic subset of the real line, and let $S$ be a saturated scalar description of $K$. Here, $c_S$ depends only on $S$ and is independent of both $F$ and the coefficient Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, which may be infinite-dimensional. In contrast to the scalar case, natural matrix preorderings admit no uniform degree bound over compact semialgebraic subsets of the real line. We construct positive semidefinite quadratic $2\times2$ matrix polynomials on unions of two intervals whose minimum certificate degrees tend to infinity as one interval shrinks to a point, while the gap remains bounded below. Conversely, uniform degree bounds hold for interval unions in a fixed compact interval when the component and gap lengths are bounded below by positive constants. Our proofs develop two techniques. The first is a quadratic reduction principle that reduces the problem of obtaining degree bounds for arbitrary-degree operator polynomials to the quadratic case, with a fixed additive increase in degree. The second uses a rank-one symmetric matrix pencil to transfer positivity on unions of intervals to $[0,1]$, where the operator Fejér-Riesz theorem provides certificates. We also obtain operator-valued Fejér-Riesz factorizations on unions of circular arcs, rational certificates with a fixed denominator on unbounded semialgebraic sets, and a characterization of the sets whose natural operator preorderings admit degree-preserving certificates.

☆ Lau's Fixed Point Problem for Elementary Amenable Groups and Finite Left Amenable Semigroups
Sławomir Borzdyński
Lau's fixed point conjecture is proved for elementary amenable groups. More generally, a weak$^*$-continuous nonexpansive representation of such a group on a nonempty weak$^*$-closed nonexpansive retract of a weak$^*$-compact convex subset $C$ of a dual Banach space has a nonempty common fixed point set that is a nonexpansive retract of $C$. For finite left amenable semigroups, continuity and weak$^*$-closedness of the retract are unnecessary. The argument also leads to a new class of amenable groups with the same retraction property, which contains all elementary amenable groups and may be strictly larger. This class may provide a useful framework for further research on Lau's conjecture. Bruck's theorem is also extended from abelian to elementary amenable group actions on nonexpansive retracts of weakly compact convex sets with the fixed point and conditional fixed point properties, without weak continuity, thus partially answering a longstanding question of Bruck. Several consequences of the theorem are recorded.

For additively coupled elements with invertible sum and selected commuting outer inverses, we study coincidence of the core idempotents and inversion of the Hua element. Intertwining forces coincidence for finite-Drazin data in unital rings and for generalized-Drazin data in complex unital Banach algebras. Under coincidence, the output splits into an invertible core and a complementary parallel sum, called the residue, yielding exact criteria for inverse existence and success of the prescribed candidate. Explicit ring examples show that strict generalized-Drazin input inverses need not force coincidence under intertwining, and that a common core with a Harte-quasinilpotent residue need not give a strict output inverse. For rings finite as modules over a commutative central subring with the same identity, we prove intertwining transfer and automatic bicommutation for commuting outer inverses with Harte-quasinilpotent remainders, without Noetherianity. This gives input-core coincidence under intertwining. If the central subring is Noetherian, every Harte-quasinilpotent element also has separated left and right powers. For common-core data in the finite-central class, the candidate is a strict output inverse exactly when the residual parallel sum is Harte-quasinilpotent. In the Banach setting, uniform input spectral gaps characterize continuity of the core and candidate along convergent input pairs, with intertwining and quasinilpotent input remainders at every term and at the limit. Let $A$ be an f-algebra and let $V$ be an order ideal of its order dual $A^{\sim}$ that separates the points of $A$. In a comment accompanying a theorem of Huijsmans and de Pagter (J. Funct. Anal. 59 (1984), 41--64), it is stated that the proof of that theorem can easily be adapted to show that the order continuous dual $V_n^{\sim}$ of $V$ is an f-algebra under the Arens multiplication. We show that this statement is false. The Arens multiplication on $V_n^{\sim}$ requires two invariance conditions on $V$, with respect to the module actions of $A$ and of $V_n^{\sim}$, which do not follow from the stated hypotheses and can fail already in the most natural case, where $A$ carries a Riesz norm and $V=A^$ is the norm dual of $A$. We prove that the first condition holds if and only if $A$ is bounded, and that the second holds whenever the Riesz norm is submultiplicative (which forces $A$ to be bounded); in that case $(A^)_n^{\sim}$ is indeed an f-algebra. We then construct a bounded f-algebra of finitely supported real sequences, equipped with a non-submultiplicative Riesz norm, for which the second condition fails, so that the Arens multiplication on $(A^*)_n^{\sim}$ is not even defined. The comment has also been used in the literature to derive a further result, which is false as well. This clarifies the exact scope of the comment.

Frames which span their underlying space using only conic combinations, known as positive spanning sets or conic frames, are of special interest in derivative free optimization. In particular, sets with large cosine measure, a measure of how spread out the vectors are, are favored. We focus on the asymptotics of the cosine measure of Gaussian frames and present tail bounds in a variety of regimes.

The second is dual and geometric, characterizing solvability via a Nehari-type distance from a cononical model-space interpolant to a subspace determined by the interpolation data. Finally, we introduce $ν$-inner functions - $ν$-Schur functions whose non-tangential boundary values lie almost everywhere in the set of extremal numerical contractions - and prove that every non-extremal problem admits a $ν$-inner solution. As a consequence, we obtain a numerical-radius Caratheodory approximation theorem: $ν$-inner functions are dense in the $ν$-Schur class under the compact-open topology.

☆ Sharp nonuniqueness for the Vlasov--Navier--Stokes system
Xingyu Li
We consider the Vlasov--Navier--Stokes system on $\mathbb T^d\times\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$. For smooth data and every $p<2$, $q<\infty$, we construct infinitely many weak solutions with velocity in $L^p_tL^\infty\cap L^1_tW^{1,q}$ and bounded, renormalized distribution function; infinitely many of them violate the energy inequality. For smooth velocity data, weak solutions with velocity in $L^2_tL^\infty$ are unique, so the result is sharp at the endpoint of the Ladyzhenskaya--Prodi--Serrin scale. The fluid carries the nonuniqueness, through the convex integration scheme of Cheskidov and Luo, and the kinetic equation is solved exactly. The main new difficulty is the memory of the particles: the kinetic state at time $t$ depends on the whole past of the velocity, so a modification on a short interval changes the system at all later times. We overcome it by a causal gluing, carried out from left to right in time, which re-solves the system on every interval of regularity. This yields wild solutions that are strong outside a closed set of times of arbitrarily small Hausdorff dimension. A causal mollification extends the construction to rough data, including every finite-energy velocity datum in dimensions two and three; in two dimensions the energy class is thus exactly the borderline of uniqueness. Finally, in three dimensions we construct Leray solutions satisfying the strong energy inequality and show that they are strong outside a closed set of times of vanishing $\mathcal H^{1/2}$ measure.

Here, using the Curie--Weiss and the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick models as prototypical examples, we show that his celebrated interpolation method is itself an optimal transport computation. After a linear change of variables the finite-$N$ pressure becomes an action $u$ with $\partial_t u = -A/2$ and $\partial_x u = -B$, where $B^2 \le A$, so $u$ is a classical subsolution of $\partial_t u+\frac12(\partial_x u)^2 \le 0$. For the Curie--Weiss model and $t > 0$, $T_t(y) = y-t\tanh y$ is an optimal transport map from every source with finite first moment if and only if $t \le 1$, and the Kantorovich potentials are the limiting pressures. For the replica-symmetric Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model, the cavity map is injective on the physical half-line and the curvature of its Brenier potential is the longitudinal eigenvalue, which exceeds the replicon eigenvalue $Λ_{\mathrm{AT}}$: transport of Dirac masses does not detect the de Almeida--Thouless line. The replicon appears along the $\mathcal{W}_2$ geodesic that splits a Dirac mass into two atoms, as the second variation of a second-order surrogate of the two-atom Parisi functional. From a Dirac initial datum, Guerra's $K$-step bound takes Hopf--Lax form, and the Parisi formula becomes a Hopf--Lax formula over atomic measures. With a $\mathcal{W}_1$-Lipschitz bound for its initial datum, proved by comparing Cole--Hopf layers, we let $K\to\infty$ and recover at Dirac data the Hopf--Lax form of the Parisi formula due to Mourrat and to Mourrat and Panchenko, with a rate for equal-mass approximations.

Above this depth, two vorticity thresholds delimit the unstable regime, outside of which the spectrum near the origin remains purely imaginary for all small Floquet exponents.
