The blow-up mechanism is a forward cascade through successively smaller scales. A main difficulty in approaching the critical exponent $1/3$ is caused by large self-deformation. Our main idea to overcome this difficulty is to obtain a lower bound for strain at the stationary non-smooth point by using angular redistribution. A related outstanding open problem is to establish an unforced Euler blow-up from smooth data in the case of axisymmetric flows with swirl. A recent multiscale construction by OpenAI for the unforced Euler equations is, however, non-axisymmetric. Although we work in the no-swirl class, the axisymmetric multiscale mechanism developed here may offer a possible route toward the still-open problem of axisymmetric smooth blow-up.

We describe a hierarchy of range failures, and demonstrate how the growth rate of~$||(A-iωI)^{-1}||_H$ dictates a regularity gap between $u$ and $f$. For super-polynomial growth, that gap can be infinite. We demonstrate this phenomenon and its equivalence to the existence of smooth resonant forces. The theory is motivated by a well-studied hyperbolic-parabolic system, which is a simplification of fluid-solid interactions. Our main result shows that, for a carefully constructed geometry, the PDE system exhibits smooth-forcing resonance for a dense set of periods. The geometry sharply violates geometric conditions for which finite regularity losses were shown previously.

Finally, we characterize the surface tensions for which further minimizers appear: this may happen only in the lamellar regime, and exactly when the Wulff shape has a corner whose normal cone contains, in its interior, a direction realizing the lattice width; in this case there are infinitely many minimizers.

We also determine the leading asymptotic profile of the solutions. Applications are given to a vector $p$-Laplacian Duffing system and to a nonsmooth problem in a Hilbert space.

The theory is motivated by a well-studied hyperbolic-parabolic system, which is a simplification of fluid-solid interactions. Our main result shows that, for a carefully constructed geometry, the PDE system exhibits smooth-forcing resonance for a dense set of periods. The geometry sharply violates geometric conditions for which finite regularity losses were shown previously.

♻ ☆ A new characterization of (pre)liminary C*-algebras
Martino Lupini
We characterize separable liminary and preliminary C*-algebras by ordinal ranks and ideal filtrations. Here liminary means that every irreducible image consists of compact operators, and preliminary means that every irreducible representation is finite dimensional. The Pedersen rank stratifies the spectrum by successive local constancy of representation dimension; Fell rank minimizes the analogous local ranks arising from positive elements. We prove that a separable type I C*-algebra is liminary if and only if its Fell rank is countable. A separable C*-algebra is preliminary if and only if it has a countable continuous ideal filtration whose successive quotients are countable direct sums of homogeneous algebras of finite representation dimension. The least possible filtration length is its Pedersen length. We also determine the possible ordinal values of the two ranks. Every nonzero countable ordinal is a Pedersen rank, whereas the nonzero countable Fell ranks are exactly $ωα+1$ and $ωλ$, where $α$ is countable and $λ$ is a nonzero countable limit ordinal. All these values occur on separable preliminary approximately finite-dimensional algebras with countable Hausdorff spectra. Among nonzero separable unital algebras, the possible Pedersen ranks of preliminary algebras are exactly the countable successors, and the possible Fell ranks of liminary algebras are exactly $ωα+1$ for countable $α$.

The separation modulus of a metric space, introduced by Bartal in 1996, is related to different notions of dimensionality. Most generally, Naor and Silberman gave in 2011 an upper bound on the separation modulus in terms of Nagata dimension. We prove that this bound cannot be reversed; that is, there are metric spaces with arbitrarily high Nagata dimension and stochastically embeddable into trees with uniform distortion, which therefore have uniformly bounded separation modulus. Similarly, we construct spaces with arbitrarily high Nagata dimension whose spaces of probability measures endowed with the Earth Mover's Distance (equivalently, their Lipschitz-free spaces) are embeddable into $L_1$ with uniformly bounded distortion. By gluing these spaces together, we obtain infinite Nagata dimensional metric spaces whose separation modulus is finite and whose Lipschitz-free space is isomorphic to $\ell_1$, respectively. Finally, we provide relations between separation modulus and stochastic embeddability into trees, also known as random approximability by tree metrics, in particular for the case of snowflake metrics.

We study the incompressible porous media (IPM) equation, a model describing the motion of a fluid with variable density through a porous medium under the action of gravity. We prove that the stably stratified state, in which heavier fluid lies below lighter fluid, is nonlinearly stable: small perturbations decay over time and the fluid returns to equilibrium. Our result holds in the sharp Sobolev setting $H^s(\mathbb R^2)$ for every $s>2$: this threshold cannot be improved, since the equation is ill-posed in $H^2(\mathbb R^2)$. This result follows from a proof of global well-posedness at critical Besov regularity, with smallness required only in a norm invariant under the natural scaling of the equation. We also prove optimal decay rates for suitably localized initial data. The main difficulty is that the stabilizing effect of stratification acts only in some directions, while the nonlinear transport acts in all of them. Reaching the sharp regularity threshold requires two main novelties. First, we rewrite the equation in \emph{isopycnal coordinates}, which follow the level sets of the density: in these coordinates the transport becomes one-dimensional, and the anisotropic stabilizing mechanism can be exploited at minimal regularity. Second, we establish new \emph{anisotropic commutator estimates} which allow us to control the remaining nonlinear terms. Finally, we show that the estimates obtained in isopycnal coordinates can be transferred back to the original variables.
♻ ☆ Global regularity and sharp decay rates for the one-dimensional hypo-viscous compressible Navier-Stokes equations in critical Besov spaces
Chen Liang, Zhaonan Luo, Zhaoyang Yin
In this paper, we study the global regularity for the one-dimensional hypo-viscous compressible Navier-Stokes equations in the critical Besov spaces, where the initial data are close to the constant equilibrium state. We introduce an effective velocity, constructed as a combination of the density and the velocity, which is used to capture the high-frequency behavior of $a$. By performing elaborate high-frequency and low-frequency estimates together with a bootstrap argument, we obtain global existence for $\frac{1}{2}\leβ<1$. In particular, when $β=\frac{1}{2}$, we also prove the system is well-posed in critical space. Furthermore, under an additional low-frequency assumption, we establish the optimal time decay rates.
♻ ☆ The $m$-Laplace equation with a gradient term I: Liouville theorem in the second subcritical case
Tian Wu, Jin Yan, Hua Zhu
Let $10$, and $p\in\mathbb R$. We study positive $C^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ weak solutions of \[-Δ_m u=u^p|Du|^q\qquad\text{in }\mathbb R^n.\] If $0
♻ ☆ The stable Bernstein theorem in $\mathbb{R}^{7}$
Han Hong, Haizhong Li, Gaoming Wang
We give a Green-function proof of the stable Bernstein theorem in $\mathbb R^7$ for smooth, connected, complete, two-sided stable minimal hypersurfaces, thus resolving the last case of the stable Bernstein problem.
comment: 47 pages. Improved exposition and simplified proofs. All comments are welcome
♻ ☆ Bilinear embedding for divergence-form operators with first-order terms and negative potentials
Lorenzo Luciano Morelato, Andrea Poggio
This article establishes a bilinear embedding for second-order divergence-form operators with complex coefficients, characterized by the simultaneous presence of first-order terms and negative potentials. This work provides a further development of the theory initiated by Carbonaro and Dragičević for the homogeneous case, and recently extended by the second author in two papers where first-order terms and negative potentials were treated separately. We work in the general setting of arbitrary open subsets of $\mathbb{R}^d$ under Dirichlet, Neumann, or mixed boundary conditions. Our main contribution is the introduction of a unified notion of generalized $p$-ellipticity that extends all its predecessors and serves as the natural condition for the bilinear inequality. Methodologically, we overcome the rigidity of the Bellman-heat method on arbitrary open subsets by introducing a novel sequence-based approach that unifies and simplifies the previous techniques. As fundamental applications, we prove the boundedness of the $H^\infty$-calculus on $L^p$ and establish $L^p$-maximal regularity. Moreover, we show that this generalized $p$-ellipticity provides a sufficient condition for the $L^p$-contractivity and $L^p$-analyticity of the generated semigroup. Finally, we apply our theory to magnetic Schrödinger operators, characterizing the range of exponents $p$ for which the associated coefficient tuple satisfies the generalized $p$-ellipticity condition introduced here.
comment: In v2 we have slightly modified the presentation of our results and added the example of magnetic Schrödinger operators; 65 pages
♻ ☆ Pitt Inequalities and Logarithmic-type Uncertainty Principles for Metaplectic Operators
Gianluca Giacchi, Itamar Oliveira, Amy Tierney
In this work, we provide a complete characterisation of Pitt's inequality for metaplectic operators. The symplectic geometry underlying a metaplectic operator distinguishes effective directions, along which its action is Fourier-type, from singular directions, along which concentration is preserved. For this reason, we adopt two complementary perspectives, thereby obtaining both an isotropic Pitt's inequality, emulating the classical theorem of Pitt, and an anisotropic inequality that adapts to the geometric features of the metaplectic group. As a by-product, we obtain Pitt's inequality for Fourier transforms along subspaces of $\rd$ and new quantitative time-dependent boundedness results for metaplectic operators on homogeneous Sobolev spaces, with applications to Schrödinger evolutions generated by quadratic Hamiltonians. Additionally, we derive logarithmic and entropic uncertainty principles for the metaplectic group. We show that the classical entropic uncertainty principle fails when both the effective and singular directions are present. In this case, a generally unbounded corrective entropy term accounts for the concentration-preserving directions and restores a meaningful lower bound. For quadratic Schrödinger evolutions, this correction follows the time-dependent geometry of the nondispersive directions and adjusts the uncertainty estimate accordingly.
comment: Journal feedback was implemented
♻ ☆ Optimizing the ground state energy of the three-dimensional magnetic Dirichlet Laplacian with constant magnetic field
Matthias Baur
This paper concerns the shape optimization problem of minimizing the ground state energy of the magnetic Dirichlet Laplacian with constant magnetic field among three-dimensional domains of fixed volume. In contrast to the two-dimensional case, a generalized "magnetic" Faber-Krahn inequality does not hold and minimizers cannot be balls when the magnetic field is turned on. An analysis of the problem among cylindrical domains reveals geometric constraints for general minimizers. In particular, minimizers must elongate with a certain rate along the direction of the magnetic field as the field strength increases. In addition to the theoretical analysis, we present numerical minimizers which confirm this prediction and give rise to further conjectures.
comment: 24 pages, 4 figures; updated to the final published version
♻ ☆ A convex integration scheme for the continuity equation past the Sobolev embedding threshold
Maria Colombo, Roberto Colombo, Anuj Kumar
We introduce a convex integration scheme for the continuity equation in the context of the Di Perna-Lions theory that allows to build incompressible vector fields in $C_{t}W^{1,p}_x$ and nonunique solutions in $C_{t} L^{q}_x$ for any $p,q$ with $\frac{1}{p} + \frac{1}{q} > 1 + \frac{1}{d}- δ$ for some $δ>0$. This improves the previous bound, corresponding to $δ=0$, or equivalently $q' > p^*$, obtained with convex integration so far, and critical for those schemes in view of the Sobolev embedding that guarantees that solutions are distributional in the opposite range.
comment: 24 pages
♻ ☆ On a fractional Alt-Caffarelli-Friedman-type monotonicity formula
Fausto Ferrari, Davide Giovagnoli, Enzo Maria Merlino
In this paper, by exploiting mean value properties of $s$-harmonic functions, we introduce some monotonicity formulas in the nonlocal setting. Our approach is purely nonlocal and does not rely on the extension technique. As a byproduct we also establish interior nonlocal gradient estimates and a nonlocal analogue of the Bochner identity.
♻ ☆ Spectral gaps and uniqueness in the isotropic $L_p$ Minkowski problem
Yao Wan
We investigate the isotropic $L_p$ Minkowski problem in $\mathbb{R}^n$ for $p<-n$. We prove that a smooth strictly convex solution $K$ is the unit ball if the second non-zero eigenvalue of the Hilbert-Brunn-Minkowski operator satisfies $λ_2(-L_K)\ge\frac{-p-1}{n-1}$. We also derive a lower bound for $λ_2(-L_K)$ in terms of concentric inner and outer ellipsoids and give improved bounds for origin-centred and origin-symmetric bodies. Combined with a weighted centroid identity for the polar body, these estimates yield an explicit $\varepsilon_n>0$ for which the unit ball is the only solution when $-n-\varepsilon_n\le p<-n$.
comment: Updated version. 21 pages. All comments are welcome
♻ ☆ Boundary value problems for 0-elliptic operators
Marco Usula
Let $X$ be a manifold with boundary, and let $L$ be a 0-elliptic operator on X which is semi-Fredholm essentially surjective with infinite-dimensional kernel. Examples include Hodge Laplacians and Dirac operators on conformally compact manifolds. We construct left and right parametrices for L when supplemented with appropriate elliptic boundary conditions. The construction relies on a new calculus of pseudodifferential operators on functions over both $X$ and $\partial X$, which we call the "symbolic 0-calculus". This new calculus supplements the ordinary 0-calculus of Mazzeo--Melrose, enabling it to handle boundary value problems. In the original 0-calculus, operators are characterized as polyhomogeneous right densities on a blow-up of $X^2$. By contrast, operators in the symbolic 0-calculus are characterized (locally near each point of the boundary of the diagonal) as quantizations of polyhomogeneous symbols on appropriate blown-up model spaces.
comment: 153 pages, 8 figures. Version published by Ars Inveniendi Analytica. Major changes from v1: 1. Addition of a "guiding example" (§2.6, §3.5, §6.5 §7.3) illustrating the theory. 2. Addition of a section (§7) with a new regularity theorem for solutions of 0-elliptic equations
♻ ☆ A Spacetime-Diffeomorphic Approach to Magnetohydrodynamics around Black Holes: Dilation Covariance, Linearization,and the No-Hair Limit
Yuanya Li
The ideal magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) system that governs a conducting plasma---the Maxwell equations together with the conservation laws of mass, momentum and energy---is the same local balance structure that describes hot accretion flows around black holes. We introduce a uniform four-dimensional spacetime dilation \[ Φ_L:\;(t',x',y',z')\mapsto (t,x,y,z)=(Lt',Lx',Ly',Lz'),\qquad L>1, \] and show that it is a smooth, orientation-preserving $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism of flat spacetime. Pulling the MHD conservation laws back through $Φ_L$, we prove that the closed ideal-MHD system is form-invariant (covariant), with the current density rescaling as $\bm j=\bm j'/L$, the magnetic diffusivity as $η'=η/L$, and external sources rescaled by $L$. The transformation realises three physically distinct effects on the perturbed flow: a \emph{linearization} to the tangent-space (linearised MHD) system, a \emph{movie slow-motion} dilation of dissipative and dynamical timescales, and an \emph{electron-microscope} magnification of small-scale structure. Taking the formal limit $L\to\infty$ localises the dynamics on a neighbourhood of a horizon: resistivity vanishes, the asymptotic time derivative freezes, and all transient multipolar structure of the infalling plasma redshifts away. The remaining stationary, axisymmetric, asymptotically flat electrovacuum is uniquely the Kerr--Newman geometry, so that the exterior of the compact object is characterised only by its mass $M$, angular momentum $J$ and charge $Q$. The result provides a local, conservation-law-based perspective on the black hole no-hair theorem that is complementary to the classical Israel--Carter-- Robinson theorems and to contemporary gravitational-wave and Event Horizon Telescope tests.
♻ ☆ Sufficient conditions for multiplicity and uniqueness of positive solutions of the Hénon equation
Geyang Du
We establish explicit sufficient conditions for multiplicity of positive solutions of the Hénon equation in the unit ball and for uniqueness in one dimension. In the Sobolev-subcritical range, a spherical harmonic function argument shows that the radial solution has Morse index greater than one and therefore differs from a ground state. In even dimensions, a degree-four perturbation in a symmetry and monotonicity cone yields a sufficient condition for nonradiality in the supercritical range. The one-dimensional uniqueness criterion follows from a comparison of weighted Dirichlet eigenvalues and a concavity estimate.
comment: 12 pages, 1 figure
♻ ☆ Global existence, blow-up behavior and numerical simulations for a class of chemotaxis-driven fish-mussel systems
Gnanasekaran Shanmugasundaram, Jitraj Saha
In this work, we investigate a chemotaxis-driven fish--mussel ecosystem model described by a coupled system of partial differential equations subject to homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions. Under suitable assumptions on the system parameters and initial data, we establish the global existence of classical solutions by employing semigroup methods together with a priori estimates. We also examine the possible blow-up behavior of solutions in a three-dimensional domain. To support the theoretical analysis, a finite element method is developed for the numerical approximation of the system, and convergence studies based on mesh refinement are carried out to verify the accuracy and stability of the proposed numerical scheme. Furthermore, numerical simulations illustrating the blow-up behavior of solutions in the computational domain are presented.
♻ ☆ Dissipative solutions for 2D Onsager's conjecture
Lili Du, Xinliang Li, Weikui Ye
In 1949, L. Onsager conjectured that weak solutions of the Euler equations in $C_{t,x}^γ$ are energy conservative when $γ>\frac{1}{3}$, whereas nonconservative solutions exist when $γ<\frac{1}{3}$. Constantin, E and Titi [13] proved the conservation part, while Isett [26] constructed nontrivial $C^γ_{t,x}$ weak solutions with compact support in time in three dimensions for each $0<γ<\frac{1}{3}$. Building on this breakthrough work, Buckmaster, De Lellis, Székelyhidi Jr. and Vicol [7] obtained strictly dissipative solutions below the Onsager threshold. In two dimensions, Giri and Radu [23] first constructed a nontrivial weak solution in $C^{\frac{1}{3}-}(\mathbb T^2\times[0,T])$ and left an open problem whether it would be possible to construct dissipative solutions (controllable energy) below $\frac{1}{3}$ threshold. In this paper, we reslove this question and thereby obtain infinitely many strictly dissipative weak solutions in $C^γ(\mathbb T^2\times[0,T])$ for every $0<γ<\frac{1}{3}$. Moreover, we prove that the associated wild initial data are dense in the divergence-free subspace of $C^{γ'}(\mathbb{T}^2)$ for any $0<γ' <\frac{1}{3}$. The key new ingredient is a family of staircase traveling waves, which we combine with a Picard iteration coupled to the Newton--Nash scheme to control both the Reynolds stress and the kinetic energy. The construction also applies in every dimension $d\geq2$.
♻ ☆ Nonlocal elliptic equations involving logarithmic Laplacian: Existence, non-existence and uniqueness results
Rakesh Arora, Jacques Giacomoni, Arshi Vaishnavi
In this work, we study the existence, non-existence, and uniqueness results for nonlocal elliptic equations involving logarithmic Laplacian, and subcritical, critical, and supercritical logarithmic nonlinearities. The Poho\u zaev's identity and Díaz-Saa type inequality are proved, which are of independent interest and can be applied to a larger class of problems. Depending upon the growth of nonlinearities and regularity of the weight function, we study the small-order asymptotic of nonlocal weighted elliptic equations involving the fractional Laplacian of order $2s.$ We show that the least energy solutions of a weighted nonlocal problem with superlinear or sublinear growth converge to a nontrivial nonnegative least-energy solution of Brézis-Nirenberg type and logistic-type limiting problem respectively involving the logarithmic Laplacian.
comment: Due to a mistake in the proof of Pohozeav identity the paper is withdrawn. A new draft is prepared with extended existence results for a large class of nonlinearity in arXiv:2504.18907.
♻ ☆ Stable solutions to $p$-Laplacian type equations with variable coefficients
Weican Luo
We study stable regular solutions of the equation $-\operatorname{div}\bigg(\Big(A(x)\nabla u \cdot \nabla u\Big)^{p/2-1}A(x)\nabla u\bigg) = f(u)$ in $B_1 \subset \mathbb{R}^n$, where $p > 1$, $f \in C^1(\mathbb{R})$ is nonnegative, and $A$ is a locally Lipschitz, symmetric, uniformly elliptic matrix field. We prove that stable regular solutions satisfy an interior Hölder estimate for $n < p + 4p/(p - 1)$ when $p \ge 2$, and for $n < 5p$ when $1 < p < 2$. This extends the result of Cabré, Miraglio, and Sanchón [7] for the $p$-Laplace equation. Note that the constant in our Hölder estimate depends on the local $C^1$ norm of $A$, but not on its $C^2$ norm. Our approach is motivated by the interior regularity estimates of Cabré, Miraglio, and Sanchón [7] for the $p$-Laplace equation and by Erneta's [14] treatment of variable coefficients in semilinear elliptic equations.
comment: 60 pages
♻ ☆ Long-time action stability for perturbed KdV near finite-gap tori
Guan Huang
We prove action and spectral stability near finite-gap tori of the periodic Korteweg--de Vries equation under autonomous analytic Hamiltonian perturbations of size $\varepsilon$. The estimates are uniform over prescribed compact families, without small-amplitude or nonresonance assumptions, and allow nearby initial data with infinitely many open gaps. Assuming a strong solution and a uniform higher Sobolev bound on $[0,T_0/\varepsilon]$, we permit one-derivative loss in the perturbing Hamiltonian's normal gradient. For sufficiently small $\varepsilon$ and initial normal Birkhoff size $r_0$, the tangential action variations and weighted sum of normal actions are bounded by $C_δ(r_0^2+\varepsilon^{2δ})$, while the spectral-gap variation in $\ell^2$ is bounded by $C_δ(r_0+\varepsilon^δ)$, for every $0<δ<1/4$. A key ingredient is coercivity of the negative Hessian of the nonlinear KdV Hamiltonian on the full $\ell^2$ action space at every finite-gap action. We combine this with resonance analysis and corrected action observables evaluated along the solution. The hypotheses are verified for several local and nonlocal Hamiltonian perturbations.
♻ ☆ Heat kernel estimates for boundary traces of reflected diffusions on uniform domains
Naotaka Kajino, Mathav Murugan
We study the boundary trace processes of reflected diffusions on uniform domains. We obtain stable-like heat kernel estimates for such a boundary trace process when the diffusion on the underlying ambient space satisfies sub-Gaussian heat kernel estimates. Our arguments rely on new results of independent interest such as sharp two-sided estimates and the volume doubling property of the harmonic measure, the existence of a continuous extension of the Naïm kernel to the topological boundary, and the Doob--Naïm formula identifying the Dirichlet form of the boundary trace process as the pure-jump Dirichlet form whose jump kernel with respect to the harmonic measure is exactly (the continuous extension of) the Naïm kernel.
comment: 129 pages; Examples 5.23 and 5.24 have been interchanged, essential errors in Example 5.24 have been corrected, and a number of minor corrections and modifications have been made
♻ ☆ Transformation of Stochastic Recursions and Critical Phenomena in the Analysis of the Athreya-Aldous-Shields Cascade and Related Mean Flow Equations
Radu Dascaliuc, Tuan N. Pham, Enrique Thomann, Edward C. Waymire
We study the discounted branching random walk process introduced by Athreya (1985) and Aldous and Shields (1988), referred to as the Athreya-Aldous-Shields (AAS) cascade. This process can be viewed as an idealized version of the stochastic model introduced by Le Jan and Sznitman in 1997 for the Navier-Stokes equations. The AAS cascade exhibits phase transitions at the critical branching rates $α=1$ and $α=2$. These transitions are reflected in the behavior of the associated mean flow equation, a nonlocal ODE referred to as the $α$-Riccati equation. It is known that if $α>1$, the AAS cascade is explosive in the sense of infinitely many splittings in finite time, and the $α$-Riccati equation has at least two solutions. In this paper, we establish finer structural properties of an explosive AAS cascade and obtain a stronger non-uniqueness result. Namely, for each initial data in a certain range, the $α$-Riccati equation has an infinite family of distinct solutions parametrized by their convergence rates at infinity. Our approach exploits a simple transformation between the AAS cascade and its "linearized" counterpart, whose mean flow equation is precisely the well-studied pantograph equation. This transformation demonstrates how a relationship at the level of stochastic processes can reveal an otherwise hidden relationship at the level of mean flow equations.
comment: 62 pages, 7 figures
♻ ☆ Finite Volume Convergence for a Heat Equation with a Measure-Valued Source
Matthias Gobbert, Martin Kružík, Andreas Meister, Michael Muscedere
Past work with Tom Seidman analyzed the spatial convergence order of the numerical finite element method applied to time-dependent diffusion-reaction equations with a measure-valued source term. For smooth source terms, the numerical method has second-order accuracy, but the non-smooth source terms introduce a limitation of the order that depends on the spatial dimension. This work in honor of Tom extends the analysis to the finite volume method in its clas- sical two-point flux form and shows that the regularity of the source term reduces the convergence order to 1 in two and 0.5 in three spatial dimensions which is reduced from the nominal second-order and depends on the space dimension. Computational tests with a point source modeled by a Dirac delta distribution exhibit the behavior predicted by the analytical results.
♻ ☆ Information geometric regularization of unidimensional pressureless Euler equations yields global strong solutions
Ruijia Cao, Florian Schäfer
Partial differential equations describing compressible fluids are prone to the formation of shock singularities, arising from faster upstream fluid particles catching up to slower, downstream ones. In geometric terms, this causes the deformation map to leave the manifold of diffeomorphisms. Information geometric regularization addresses this issue by changing the manifold geometry to make it geodesically complete. Empirical evidence suggests that this results in smooth solutions without adding artificial viscosity. This work makes a first step towards understanding this phenomenon rigorously, in the setting of the unidimensional pressureless Euler equations. It shows that their information geometric regularization has smooth global solutions. By establishing $Γ$-convergence of its variational description, it proves convergence of these solutions to entropy solutions of the nominal problem, in the limit of vanishing regularization parameter. A consequence of these results is that manifolds of unidimensional diffeomorphisms with information geometric regularization are geodesically complete.
Functional Analysis
☆ Hardy Spaces and Toeplitz operators on the Hexablock
Sourav Pal, Guicong Su, Nitin Tomar
The hexablock is a domain in $\mathbb{C}^4$ given by \[ \mathbb{H}=\left\{(a,x_1,x_2,x_3)\in \mathbb{C}\times\mathbb{E}: \sup_{z_1,z_2\in\mathbb{D}} \left| \frac{a\sqrt{(1-|z_1|^2)(1-|z_2|^2)}} {1-x_1z_1-x_2z_2+x_3z_1z_2} \right|<1 \right\}, \] where $\mathbb{E}=\left\{(x_1,x_2,x_3)\in\mathbb{C}^{3}: 1-x_1z_1-x_2z_2+x_3z_1z_2\neq 0 \ \text{for all}\ z_1,z_2\in\overline{\mathbb D}\right\}$ is the tetrablock. We introduce a Hardy space $H^2(\mathbb H)$ associated with a canonical measure $μ_{\mathbb H}$ on the distinguished boundary $b\mathbb H$ of the hexablock. We identify $H^2(\mathbb H)$ with a closed subspace of $L^2(b\mathbb H,μ_{\mathbb H})$ and show that it is a reproducing kernel Hilbert space. We prove that $\mathbb H$ is the interior of the polynomial convex hull of $Ψ_{\mathbb H}(\overline{\mathbb D}^4)$, where \[ Ψ_{\mathbb H}(ξ_1, ξ_2,λ_1,λ_2) = \left(\frac{λ_1(ξ_1-1)}{2}, \frac{ξ_2(ξ_1+1)}{2}, \ \frac{λ_1λ_2(ξ_1+1)}{2}, \ ξ_1 ξ_2λ_1λ_2 \right). \] We obtain a Brown-Halmos type characterization of Toeplitz operators on $H^2(\mathbb H)$ and a commutant lifting theorem for $\mathbb H$-isometries. We characterize $\mathbb H$-unitaries as the images of commuting quadruples of unitaries under $Ψ_{\mathbb H}$ and present a class of $\mathbb H$-contractions from commuting quadruples having $\overline{\mathbb D}^4$ as a spectral set. We prove an analogous characterization of $\mathbb E$-unitaries and present a class of $\mathbb E$-contractions arising from commuting triples of contractions having $\overline{\mathbb D}^3$ as a spectral set. En route, we also study a weighted Hardy space on the hexablock.

☆ Augmented Dynamical Sampling under unmodeled Forcing
Juan Giribet, Serena Feldberg
We study recovery of an initial state from dynamical samples of a trajectory driven by unknown additive forcing. Measurements against both the original sensors and their images under the adjoint nominal evolution yield one-step residuals that cancel the initial state exactly. These residuals separate forcing estimation from initial-state reconstruction. For a centered Gaussian forcing model with fixed covariance parameters, we combine Gaussian conditioning with canonical dual-frame reconstruction and derive an exact unconditional second-moment identity, including the correlation between the forcing-estimation error and the measurement noise. We also obtain high-probability bounds and identify the irreducible forcing uncertainty through a conditional covariance in the geometry induced by the prior. A hierarchy of augmented sensor systems separates the role of sampling depth in forcing visibility from that of the observation horizon in nominal observability. An image-transport experiment and finite-dimensional and periodic-convolution experiments illustrate the residual correction and the separate roles of sampling depth and observation horizon.
☆ Quantitative characterization of Gaussian small ball probabilities
Jaouad Mourtada
The quantitative study of the Gaussian measure of symmetric convex sets is a central theme at the interface of probability theory and convex geometry. From a probabilistic perspective, it amounts to analyzing the tail behavior of suprema of Gaussian processes. The typical magnitude and upper tail of Gaussian processes are well-understood, thanks to Talagrand's celebrated Majorizing Measures theorem and to Gaussian concentration. In contrast, despite fundamental connections with metric entropy established by Kuelbs and Li, no general sharp characterization of the lower tail is available. In this work, we close this gap by establishing a sharp two-sided characterization of Gaussian small ball probabilities, involving both metric entropy and local widths of the underlying convex body. This yields an explicit chaining-type description of lower quantiles of Gaussian processes in terms of the metric structure of the convexified index set, as well as a general comparison inequality for convex sets. We further obtain analogous quantitative characterizations of two important geometric quantities associated with symmetric convex sets, namely intrinsic volumes (quermassintegrals) and the radii of random sections beyond the classical Dvoretzky range. A unifying theme of these results is the central role of convexity in the quantitative understanding of small ball probabilities.
comment: 63 pages
☆ The Brown--Shields Conjecture: Two Approximation Theorems and a Counterexample
Bonan Chen, Xiang Fang, Feng Guo
We construct an outer function in the classical Dirichlet space whose radial zero set has logarithmic capacity zero, but whose polynomial multiples do not approximate the constant function $1$. This disproves the Brown--Shields conjecture. The proof rests on two approximation theorems for canonical generators of invariant subspaces. The first shows that every proper outer canonical generator can be approximated in the Dirichlet norm by canonical generators associated with singular inner functions determined by finite positive atomic measures. The second shows that each fixed finite-atomic canonical generator can be recovered as a strong Dirichlet limit of outer canonical generators whose radial zero sets have arbitrarily small logarithmic capacity. We then combine these approximations using two techniques: a complete metric that controls boundary logarithms and a nested-ball construction that preserves outerness and noncyclicity while ensuring that the radial zero set is polar. In fact, we show that every proper outer canonical generator can be approximated arbitrarily closely by such counterexamples, both in the Dirichlet norm and in the $L^1$ norm of their boundary logarithms.

☆ Kac lemma on noncommutative probability spaces
Tattwamasi Amrutam, Diptesh Saha, Xumin Wang
We prove non-commutative Kac's formula for actions of countable groups. We replace the return time functions by suitable projections in von Neumann algebras. Moreover, we prove a generalised Kac's formula in the non-commutative setting which extends the allocation construction of Meyerovitch and Weiss and is motivated by the random Kac inequality of Aaronson.
comment: 19 pages; preliminary version. Comments are welcome
☆ Three Lipschitz functions on infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces with no common point of Fréchet differentiability
Zhouzhe Wang
We prove that on every infinite-dimensional real Hilbert space \(H\), there exist three real-valued Lipschitz functions with no common point of Fréchet differentiability. This gives a negative answer to a longstanding question of Lindenstrauss, Preiss, and Tišer. The proof is constructive and relies on elementary calculus and finite-dimensional linear algebra. Since every Lipschitz map from a Hilbert space into $\mathbb R^2$ has a point of Fréchet differentiability, the target dimension three is optimal.
☆ Invariant subspaces for integration and differentiation on convex domains
Erik Avelin
For a conformal map $g$ of the unit disc $U$ onto any bounded convex domain $Ω$ we determine the invariant subspaces for the integration operator $T_gf = \int_0^zfg'$ on the Hardy space $H^p$, by means of a Fock space model. Under some additional regularity assumptions on $\partialΩ$ we also treat integration from a boundary point of $U$, and we determine the residual subspaces (those invariant subspaces on which the operator has empty spectrum) for the left inverse $D_gf = f'/g'$ of $T_g$ on the smooth disc algebra $A^\infty$. The latter result is new even for $Ω= U$.
☆ Analogs of crystalline measures in tube sets
Özkan Deǧer, Sergii Favorov
Let $μ$ be a pure point complex measure on a tube set $R^d+i F$, where $F$ is a compact convex subset in $R^d$, such that this tube set is the minimal closed convex tube set containing support of $μ$. Furthermore, assume that the Fourier transform $\hatμ$ (in the sense of distributions) is a measure. We determine conditions on the measure $μ$ under which the variation of the measure $\hatμ$ grows at least as $\exp\{2πH_F(t)\}$, as well as conditions under which this variation grows at most as $\exp\{2πH_F(t)\}$; here $H_F(t)$ is the support function of $F$.
comment: 16 pages, 20 references
☆ Weighted STSAFT-Modulation Spaces and Approximation by Phase-Adapted Neural Networks
Ming Hu, Bei Liu, Bolin Liu, Jie Shen
We develop a transform-adapted approximation framework for shallow neural networks based on the short-time special affine Fourier transform (STSAFT). Replacing the short-time Fourier transform (STFT) in the definition of classical modulation spaces, we work with weighted STSAFT-modulation spaces, building on the existing SAFT-associated modulation-space framework, and use their chirp correspondence with classical weighted modulation spaces through the chirp factorization of the SAFT kernel. We construct an associated neural dictionary and establish an $N$-term Sobolev approximation bound of order $N^{-1/2}$ on bounded one-dimensional domains. A global approximation theorem is also obtained when the spatial translation parameter ranges over the whole real line; a compact-support argument explains why an unrestricted global conclusion cannot in general be inferred from a bounded translation range. For a fixed-scale chirp family $f_κ(x)=e^{iπκx^2}u(x)$, we combine the global estimate with a phase analysis to obtain the stronger phase-dependent upper-bound factor $\langleλ\rangle^n\langleκ-λ\rangle^{n+3/2-1/r}.$ For each fixed nonzero Schwartz envelope, matching the dictionary phase reduces the growth of this specified upper bound from order $|κ|^{n+3/2-1/r}$ to order $|κ|^n$, while preserving the $N^{-1/2}$ rate. The associated mismatch scale is stated as a comparison of upper bounds, not as a threshold for the optimal approximation error. Four numerical experiments examine model comparison, error decay with dictionary size, phase mismatch, and the obstruction caused by restricted translations. We discuss the effective number of fitted output coefficients, including the rank loss of the sine branch at zero phase, and distinguish the numerical diagnostics from the theoretical best-approximation estimates.

☆ Convolution on quantum tori I: Sharp Young inequalities and endpoint Sobolev embeddings
Fedor Sukochev, Ramazan Tastankul, Kanat Tulenov, Dmitriy Zanin
We introduce a convolution of noncommutative tori. The construction is the preadjoint of a trace-preserving cocycle-addition homomorphism. Its zero-parameter case is the function--operator semi-convolution. We prove both mixed $L_{1}$--$L_\infty$ inequalities and various Young inequalities with the optimal constant one, including their limiting cases. The endpoint bounds also yield submajorization and convolution estimates in fully symmetric spaces. As applications, we establish, for every integer $k\geq1$ and $1\leq p\leq\infty$, $W_{p}^{k}(\mathbb{T}_θ^{d})\hookrightarrow B_{\infty,\infty}^{k-\frac{d}{p}}(\mathbb{T}_θ^{d})$, and prove the critical embedding $W_{1}^{d}(\mathbb{T}_θ^{d})\hookrightarrow L_\infty(\mathbb{T}_θ^{d})$. These results settle the two questions posed in Remark~6.8 of Xiong, Xu and Yin \cite{XiongXuYin}.
☆ The Triangular Abrikosov Constant and the Thomas--Fermi $Γ$-Limit of Rotating Bose--Einstein Condensates
Giovanni Di Fratta, Valeriy V. Slastikov
We resolve the Abrikosov coefficient conjecture for rapidly rotating two-dimensional Bose--Einstein condensates within the variational framework of $Γ$-convergence. For a harmonic trap, we establish the $Γ$-convergence of the rescaled Gross--Pitaevskii energy functionals in the fast-rotation regime, through weak $L^2$ convergence of the rescaled densities, and identify the effective interaction coefficient $β_*$ with $b_\triangle$, the Abrikosov ratio associated with the triangular vortex lattice. The limiting Thomas--Fermi functional determines the first correction to the minimum energy and the macroscopic density of almost minimizers. For the auxiliary rescaled model and its lowest-Landau-level restriction, we also compute a strictly positive limiting $L^2$ distance between minimizing densities and the Thomas--Fermi profile. The identification of the effective interaction coefficient $β_*$ with the triangular Abrikosov ratio $b_\triangle$ relies on the sharp Gaussian-minorant theorem established in a recent OpenAI preprint~\cite[Theorem~1.2]{Atomic}. A Fourier representation of the quartic energy and a weighted Poisson identity yield a lower bound for arbitrary magnetic-periodic lowest-Landau-level states. The sign conditions on the minorant and its Fourier transform give the bound, while the lattice contact conditions identify its coefficient with $b_\triangle$. Cutoff and magnetic projection transfer this estimate to local holomorphic states without boundary conditions or periodicity assumptions. Consequently, the free-cell coefficients converge to $b_\triangle$ with error $O(L^{-1/5})$ on squares of side length $L$.
comment: 47 pages, 3 Figures
☆ Noncommutative Rational Positivstellensätze with Operator Coefficients
Abhay Jindal, Igor Klep, Jurij Volčič
We establish a convex Positivstellensatz for noncommutative rational functions with bounded operator coefficients. A hermitian operator-valued rational function that is positive semidefinite on a matrix convex set described by a linear pencil admits a positivity certificate consisting of rational hermitian squares and a completely positive term involving the defining linear pencil. The certificate comes with an explicit complexity bound independent of the dimension of the coefficient Hilbert space. As a consequence, we solve the operator-valued noncommutative rational analog of Hilbert's 17th problem: every positive semidefinite operator-valued noncommutative rational function is a sum of hermitian squares, and even a single hermitian square when the coefficient Hilbert space is infinite-dimensional. In contrast, the corresponding commutative statement fails for infinite-dimensional operator coefficients.
☆ Composition operators on weighted Beurling--Sobolev spaces
Stéphane Charpentier, Rachid Zarouf
Given a function $\varphi:\D\to \D$ holomorphic in a neighborhood of the closed unit disk $\overline{\D}$, we study the matrix \[ A_\varphi = \big(\widehat{\varphi^n}(k)\big)_{n,k\geq 0}. \] We obtain a complete characterization of those $\varphi$ for which $A_\varphi$ acts boundedly from $\ell^p$ to $\ell^q$, $p,q\in [1,\infty]$. These results can be reformulated in terms of composition operators, providing a complete description of the symbols $\varphi$ holomorphic in a neighbourhood of $\overline{\D}$ that induce a bounded composition operator $C_\varphi:f\mapsto f\circ \varphi$ between two possibly different Beurling--Sobolev spaces. In particular, we prove that $C_\varphi$ is bounded on $\ell_a^p$ for some $p\neq 2$ if and only if it is bounded on every $\ell_a^p$, $p\in [1,\infty]$, if and only if $\varphi$ satisfies an analytic condition at the points of $\overline{\D}$ where it touches the unit circle. Extensions to weighted Beurling--Sobolev spaces are also provided.
♻ ☆ Structured coordinate systems in $L^p(\mathbb{R})$
Daniel Freeman, Lukas Liehr, Mitchell A. Taylor
We construct Schauder bases of $L^p(\mathbb{R})$ with significant structural constraints on their elements. For every $1 \leq p< \infty$, we obtain bases of non-negative functions with basis constants arbitrarily close to one, as well as bases with positive biorthogonal functionals. For every $2 \leq p < \infty$, we construct Schauder bases consisting of translates of a single function, which can be chosen to extend to an entire function. When $p>2$, the translation parameters can be chosen from any prescribed unbounded subset of $\mathbb{R}$, a conclusion that fails for $p=2$. Finally, for $p>2$, the entire function generating the basis of translates can also be chosen non-negative.
♻ ☆ Frame constructions associated with operator orbits
Eva A. Gallardo-Gutiérrez, Jonathan R. Partington
This paper studies frames in Hilbert spaces generated by the orbits of finitely many vectors under a single operator, presenting new results on normal operators and multiplication operators as well as on operators composed of Jordan blocks. These results generalize existing results of Cabrelli, Molter, Paternostro and Philipp by means of techniques which deal with weighted interpolation, weighted composition operators, and Beurling--Lax theory related to shifts of finite multiplicity. Likewise, we discuss Carleson frames and construct counterexamples to a recent conjecture of Aldroubi, Cabrelli, Krishtal and Molter, showing that the relevant necessary condition is of density type rather than the Müntz--Szász condition. Moreover, by using the theory of weighted composition operators, we answer a question of Cheshmavar on frames produced by iterative multiplication. Finally, for orbits of infinitely many vectors the underlying model is a shift of infinite multiplicity which, by a theorem of Rota, is a universal operator; consequently, a complete description of such frames along these lines would encompass the Invariant Subspace Problem.

In this paper we study the necessary and sufficient conditions on domain for Musielak-Orlicz-Sobolev embedding of the space $W^{1,Φ(\cdot,\cdot)}(Ω)$ where $Φ(x,t):=t^{p(x)}{(\log(e+t))}^{q(x)}.$

♻ ☆ Translation Continuity and the Structure of Infinite-Dimensional Lebesgue Spaces
Daniel L. Rodríguez-Vidanes, Juan Carlos Sampedro
For Baker's Borel-rectangle measure $μ$ and $1\le p<\infty$, we classify the continuous vectors of each one-parameter translation group on $L^p(μ)$. For each $v\in\mathbb{R}^\mathbb{N}$, the continuous vectors form a projection band, which coincides with the whole space when $v$ has finite support, is trivial when $v\notin\ell^1$, and is nonzero and proper otherwise. We also establish in ZFC the isometric classification considered in [Isometric classification of the $L^{p}$-spaces of infinite dimensional Lebesgue measure, Banach J. Math. Anal. 20 (2026), no. 1, Paper No. 7], showing that both $L^p(μ)$ and the kernel of restriction to integer cubes are lattice isometric to $\ell^p(\mathfrak{c},L^p[0,1])$. When $v\in\ell^1\setminus c_{00}$, the continuous band and its disjoint complement have the same lattice-isometric structure, with the latter contained in the cube-restriction kernel.
♻ ☆ The Bishop--Phelps--Bollobás Property for Extremally Disconnected Ranges
Tattwamasi Amrutam, Priyadarshi Dey, Chunlin Liu, Monika
Let $\mathbb F$ be either $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, and let $L$ be a nonempty extremally disconnected compact Hausdorff space. We show that $(X,C(L,\mathbb F))$ has the Bishop--Phelps--Bollobás property with $η(\varepsilon)=\varepsilon^2/2$ for every Banach space $X$ over $\mathbb F$. For each fixed $L$ and either scalar field, this bound is optimal uniformly over $X$.

♻ ☆ The linear scale in metric cotype for Alexandrov spaces of nonnegative curvature
Longfa Sun, Yipeng Zhang
We answer a question of Eskenazis, Mendel, and Naor by proving that the optimal universal scaling parameter in metric cotype $2$ for complete Alexandrov spaces of nonnegative curvature has order $n$. The upper bound follows from a dyadic application of the Lang--Schroeder inequality, and the lower bound follows from snowflake universality of $\mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb{R}^3)$.

♻ ☆ Crossed-Heinz Inequalities
Mohammad Sababheh, Jean-Christophe Bourin
For positive matrices $A,B$ and $p,q>0$, the second author (2009) asked whether the inequality \[ \|A^pB^q+B^pA^q\|\leq \|A^{p+q}+B^{p+q}\| \] holds for every unitarily invariant norm. Despite a series of papers addressing this question, as well as recent intensive computational and AI-assisted investigations by Matthew Colbrook (2026, \cite{Col}), the problem remains open. It is a striking example of how an elementary scalar statement can become extremely difficult to handle in the noncommutative setting. Some partial positive results are known. In this note, we provide one more: the crossed-Heinz inequality holds for two-by-two matrices. This result also leads to a new and elegant characterization of the singular values of two-by-two matrices. In arbitrary dimension, we turn to the special case $p=q=1$, obtaining a series of eigenvalue estimates for the anticommutator $AB+BA$.
comment: This paper has been accepted for publication in the Bulletin of the Australian Mathematical Society
♻ ☆ Bilinear embedding for divergence-form operators with first-order terms and negative potentials
Lorenzo Luciano Morelato, Andrea Poggio
This article establishes a bilinear embedding for second-order divergence-form operators with complex coefficients, characterized by the simultaneous presence of first-order terms and negative potentials. This work provides a further development of the theory initiated by Carbonaro and Dragičević for the homogeneous case, and recently extended by the second author in two papers where first-order terms and negative potentials were treated separately. We work in the general setting of arbitrary open subsets of $\mathbb{R}^d$ under Dirichlet, Neumann, or mixed boundary conditions. Our main contribution is the introduction of a unified notion of generalized $p$-ellipticity that extends all its predecessors and serves as the natural condition for the bilinear inequality. Methodologically, we overcome the rigidity of the Bellman-heat method on arbitrary open subsets by introducing a novel sequence-based approach that unifies and simplifies the previous techniques. As fundamental applications, we prove the boundedness of the $H^\infty$-calculus on $L^p$ and establish $L^p$-maximal regularity. Moreover, we show that this generalized $p$-ellipticity provides a sufficient condition for the $L^p$-contractivity and $L^p$-analyticity of the generated semigroup. Finally, we apply our theory to magnetic Schrödinger operators, characterizing the range of exponents $p$ for which the associated coefficient tuple satisfies the generalized $p$-ellipticity condition introduced here.
comment: In v2 we have slightly modified the presentation of our results and added the example of magnetic Schrödinger operators; 65 pages
♻ ☆ The Gleason--Kahane--Zelazko theorem: a gentle introduction
Catalin Badea
After some personal recollections of Jean-Pierre Kahane, this paper gives a gentle introduction to the Gleason-Kahane-Zelazko theorem. The theorem states that a normalised complex-linear functional on a unital complex Banach algebra is multiplicative whenever it does not vanish on invertible elements. Neither continuity of the functional nor commutativity of the algebra is assumed. We give a detailed account of three proofs: the original argument of Gleason and, independently, Kahane and Zelazko; the polynomial proof of Roitman and Sternfeld; and a proof by the author. We explain the complex analysis behind each: a special case of Hadamard's factorisation theorem, a polynomial argument using the fundamental theorem of algebra, and the Polya-Saxer theorem on zero-free entire functions and their derivatives. The elementary entire-function lemma needed for the first proof is proved in full; the Polya-Saxer theorem is used without proof. We give full details of the algebraic argument common to the three proofs, which deduces multiplicativity from the preservation of squares, including the non-commutative case. We then discuss applications and counterexamples, and present an extension to Ransford's generalised spectra using the Roitman--Sternfeld argument. We conclude with a brief guide to the more recent literature.
comment: 31 pages. Paper submitted to a volume in memory of Jean-Pierre Kahane
♻ ☆ Invariance Preserving Conjugation and Linear Operators on the Hardy Space
Arup Chattopadhyay, Supratim Jana
We study linear and anti-linear operators on the Hardy space $H^2$ in connection with the Beurling lattice. First, in contrast to Sarason's result \cite{S1}, we show that no non-zero anti-linear operator leaves every shift-invariant subspace invariant. Then we completely characterize the class of conjugations, isometries, and invertible linear operators preserving the shift-invariant subspace structure in terms of weighted composition operators induced by disk automorphisms--combined with the canonical conjugation, isometric multiplication, and invertible Toeplitz operators, respectively. We also establish the existence and non-existence of conjugations that map shift-invariant subspaces to coinvariant subspaces. Finally, we construct a counterexample that rules out an analogous factorization for bounded linear operators preserving shift-invariance of closed images.
comment: Thoroughly revised. Comments are welcome
♻ ☆ Fast approximation and learning of binary classification tasks in o-minimal structures using ReLU neural networks
Clemens Kinn, Philipp Petersen
We study binary classification tasks whose decision sets are given by definable sets in o-minimal expansions of the real field. Motivated by the cell decomposition theory of definable sets, we introduce traceable sets that isolate the analytical properties of definable sets used for fast approximation by ReLU neural networks. Under uniform bounds on the number of cells and a suitable extension assumption for the boundary functions, we prove that classifiers can be approximated in $L^p$ up to accuracy $\varepsilon>0$ by ReLU neural networks of size $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-p(n-1)/m})$, with depth independent of $\varepsilon$ and polynomially bounded weights. This establishes quantitative approximation rates for suitable definable collections in o-minimal structures using ReLU neural networks. Furthermore, the stated approximation rates are also derived for definable maps under similar geometric assumptions on their smoothness domains. We then obtain statistical learning rates for empirical risk minimization with hinge loss over the approximating ReLU neural network classes. For $N$ uniformly distributed samples, the predicted classifiers achieve expected misclassification error of order $N^{-m/(m+n-1)}$ up to an arbitrarily small polynomial loss.
♻ ☆ Improvement of a Hardy-Littlewood inequality and applications to the boundedness of analytic paraproducts on mixed norm spaces
Álvaro Miguel Moreno, José Ángel Peláez
Let $\mathcal{H}(\mathbb{D})$ denote the space of analytic functions in the unit disc $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$. For $0
♻ ☆ Banach-Valued Carré du Champ Operators and Functional Gaussian Approximation
Solesne Bourguin, Simon Campese
We develop a projective-tensor-valued carré du champ for Malliavin-differentiable Banach-valued random elements and establish an associated integration-by-parts formula. The resulting dimension-free comparison principle bounds Gaussian approximation against twice Fréchet-differentiable test functions by the expected projective norm of a random covariance discrepancy. For processes on Skorokhod space equipped with the uniform norm, a smoothing argument converts this comparison into a quantitative bound in the bounded-Lipschitz metric, subject to explicit regularization errors. On Banach-valued Wiener chaos we express the carré du champ through contractions and obtain quantitative estimates in terms of contracted kernels. As a concrete application, we establish a quantitative functional Breuer--Major bound for the canonical polygonally interpolated partial-sum process, together with a corollary for the original Skorokhod step process. The estimate applies to the entire path in the uniform topology under explicit covariance conditions. We also record the trace-class specialization of the contraction bounds in Hilbert spaces.
♻ ☆ The Strong Naor--Schechtman Convolution Inequality on the Product of Cyclic Groups
Yong Jiao, Sijie Luo, Dmitriy Zanin, Dejian Zhou
In this paper, we resolve the convolution inequality problem posed by Naor and Schechtman in \cite[Question 6.1]{N-S2016} (see also \cite{Na2016}). More precisely, we establish the following strong convolution inequality on products of finite cyclic groups: For each $1\leq p<\infty$ there exists $c_{p}>0$ such that for every $n$, $m\in \mathbb{N}$ the following holds \[ \begin{split} &\sum_{\varepsilon\in \{-1,1\}^{n}}\sum_{x\in \Z}\left|E_{\{1,\cdots,n\}}f(x+\varepsilon)-E_{\{1,\cdots,n\}}f(x-\varepsilon)\right|^{p}\\ \leq& c^{p}_{p}\sum_{\varepsilon\in \{-1,1\}^{n}}\sum_{x\in \Z}\left|\varepsilon_{j}\left[E_{\{1,\cdots,n\}\setminus\{j\}}f(x+e_{j})-E_{\{1,\cdots,n\}\setminus\{j\}}f(x-e_{j})\right]\right|^{p}, \end{split} \] $E_{A}f(x)=\frac{1}{2^{n}}\sum_{δ\in \{-1,1\}^{n}}f\left(x+\sum_{j\in A}δ_{j}e_{j}\right)$ for every $A\subseteq \{1,\cdots,n\}$. The growth order we obtain here $c_{p}=O(p)$ as $p\to \infty$. For the endpoint $p=\infty$, we show by a counterexample that the strong convolution inequality fails for the $L_{\infty}$, and we prove that the appropriate endpoint for $p=\infty$ is the martingale $BMO$ space.
